20:2.en: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed

20:3.en: But as a reminder unto him who feareth

20:4.ar: تَنزِيلࣰ ا مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلۡعُلَى
20:4.en: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens

20:5.en: The Beneficent One, Who is established on the Throne

20:6.ar: لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحۡتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
20:6.en: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and whatsoever is between them, and whatsoever is beneath the sod

20:7.ar: وَإِن تَجۡهَرۡ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَعۡلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخۡفَى
20:7.en: And if thou speakest aloud, then lo! He knoweth the secret (thought) and (that which is yet) more hidden

20:8.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ
20:8.en: Allah! There is no Allah save Him. His are the most beautiful names

20:9.en: Hath there come unto thee the story of Moses

20:10.ar: إِذۡ رَءَا نَارࣰ ا فَقَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّيٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنۡهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوۡ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدࣰ ى
20:10.en: When he saw a fire and said unto his folk: Lo! Wait! I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom or may find guidance at the fire

20:11.en: And when he reached it, he was called by name: O Moses

20:12.ar: إِنِّيٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخۡلَعۡ نَعۡلَيۡكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسِ طُوࣰ ى
20:12.en: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa

20:13.en: And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired

20:14.ar: إِنَّنِيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعۡبُدۡنِي وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكۡرِيٓ
20:14.en: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no Allah save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance

20:15.ar: إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخۡفِيهَا لِتُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا تَسۡعَىٰ
20:15.en: Lo! the Hour is surely coming. But I will to keep it hidden, that every soul may be rewarded for that which it striveth (to achieve)

20:16.ar: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنۡهَا مَن لَّا يُؤۡمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرۡدَىٰ
20:16.en: Therefor, let not him turn thee aside from (the thought of) it who believeth not therein but followeth his own desire, lest thou perish

20:17.en: And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses

20:18.ar: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُاْ عَلَيۡهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخۡرَىٰ
20:18.en: He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses

20:19.en: He said: Cast it down, O Moses

20:20.en: So he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent, gliding

20:21.ar: قَالَ خُذۡهَا وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلۡأُولَىٰ
20:21.en: He said: Grasp it and fear not. We shall return it to its former state

20:22.ar: وَٱضۡمُمۡ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخۡرُجۡ بَيۡضَآءَ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخۡرَىٰ
20:22.en: And thrust thy hand within thine armpit, it will come forth white without hurt. (That will be) another token

20:23.en: That We may show thee (some) of Our greater portents

20:24.en: Go thou unto Pharaoh! Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds)

20:25.en: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind

20:26.en: And ease my task for me

20:27.en: And loose a knot from my tongue

20:28.en: That they may understand my saying

20:29.ar: وَٱجۡعَل لِّي وَزِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِي
20:29.en: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk

20:32.en: And let him share my task

20:33.en: That we may glorify Thee much

20:35.en: Lo! Thou art ever Seeing us

20:36.en: He said: Thou art granted thy request, O Moses

20:37.en: And indeed, another time, already We have shown thee favour

20:38.ar: إِذۡ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
20:38.en: When we inspired in thy mother that which is inspired

20:39.ar: أَنِ ٱقۡذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقۡذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ فَلۡيُلۡقِهِ ٱلۡيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأۡخُذۡهُ عَدُوࣱّ لِّي وَعَدُوࣱّ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَلۡقَيۡتُ عَلَيۡكَ مَحَبَّةࣰ مِّنِّي وَلِتُصۡنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيۡنِيٓ
20:39.en: Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will

20:40.ar: إِذۡ تَمۡشِيٓ أُخۡتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكۡفُلُهُۥۖ فَرَجَعۡنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَيۡ تَقَرَّ عَيۡنُهَا وَلَا تَحۡزَنَۚ وَقَتَلۡتَ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَنَجَّيۡنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونࣰ اۚ فَلَبِثۡتَ سِنِينَ فِيٓ أَهۡلِ مَدۡيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئۡتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرࣲ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
20:40.en: When thy sister went and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him? and we restored thee to thy mother that her eyes might be refreshed and might not sorrow. And thou didst kill a man and We delivered thee from great distress, and tried thee with a heavy trial. And thou didst tarry years among the folk of Midian. Then camest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses

20:41.en: And I have attached thee to Myself

20:42.ar: ٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَٰتِي وَلَا تَنِيَا فِي ذِكۡرِي
20:42.en: Go, thou and thy brother, with My tokens, and be not faint in remembrance of Me

20:43.en: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds)

20:44.ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا لَّيِّنࣰ ا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ
20:44.en: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear

20:45.ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفۡرُطَ عَلَيۡنَآ أَوۡ أَن يَطۡغَىٰ
20:45.en: They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us or that he may play the tyrant

20:46.ar: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآۖ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَآ أَسۡمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
20:46.en: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing

20:47.ar: فَأۡتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَا بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡۖ قَدۡ جِئۡنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكَۖ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
20:47.en: So go ye unto him and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord. So let the children of Israel go with us, and torment them not. We bring thee a token from thy Lord. And peace will be for him who followeth right guidance

20:48.ar: إِنَّا قَدۡ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡنَآ أَنَّ ٱلۡعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
20:48.en: Lo! it hath been revealed unto us that the doom will be for him who denieth and turneth away

20:49.en: (Pharaoh) said: Who then is the Lord of you twain, O Moses

20:50.ar: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِيٓ أَعۡطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلۡقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
20:50.en: He said: Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its nature, then guided it aright

20:51.en: He said: What then is the state of the generations of old

20:52.ar: قَالَ عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَٰبࣲۖ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنسَى
20:52.en: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither erreth nor forgetteth

20:53.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَهۡدࣰ ا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا سُبُلࣰ ا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا مِّن نَّبَاتࣲ شَتَّىٰ
20:53.en: Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads for you therein and hath sent down water from the sky and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds of vegetation

20:54.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱرۡعَوۡاْ أَنۡعَٰمَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّأُوْلِي ٱلنُّهَىٰ
20:54.en: (Saying): Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought

20:55.ar: ۞مِنۡهَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمۡ وَمِنۡهَا نُخۡرِجُكُمۡ تَارَةً أُخۡرَىٰ
20:55.en: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time

20:56.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
20:56.en: And We verily did show him all Our tokens, but he denied them and refused

20:57.ar: قَالَ أَجِئۡتَنَا لِتُخۡرِجَنَا مِنۡ أَرۡضِنَا بِسِحۡرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
20:57.en: He said: Hast come to drive us out from our land by thy magic, O Moses

20:58.ar: فَلَنَأۡتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحۡرࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦ فَٱجۡعَلۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكَ مَوۡعِدࣰ ا لَّا نُخۡلِفُهُۥ نَحۡنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانࣰ ا سُوࣰ ى
20:58.en: But we surely can produce for thee magic the like thereof; so appoint a tryst between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both)

20:59.ar: قَالَ مَوۡعِدُكُمۡ يَوۡمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحۡشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحࣰ ى
20:59.en: (Moses) said: Your tryst shall be the day of the feast, and let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high

20:60.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيۡدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
20:60.en: Then Pharaoh went and gathered his strength, then came (to the appointed tryst)

20:61.ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيۡلَكُمۡ لَا تَفۡتَرُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا فَيُسۡحِتَكُم بِعَذَابࣲۖ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ
20:61.en: Moses said unto them: Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you by some punishment. He who lieth faileth miserably

20:62.en: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their counsel secret

20:63.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَٰنِ لَسَٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخۡرِجَاكُم مِّنۡ أَرۡضِكُم بِسِحۡرِهِمَا وَيَذۡهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلۡمُثۡلَىٰ
20:63.en: They said: Lo! these are two wizards who would drive you out from your country by their magic, and destroy your best traditions

20:64.ar: فَأَجۡمِعُواْ كَيۡدَكُمۡ ثُمَّ ٱئۡتُواْ صَفࣰّ اۚ وَقَدۡ أَفۡلَحَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مَنِ ٱسۡتَعۡلَىٰ
20:64.en: So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful

20:65.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلۡقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰ
20:65.en: They said: O Moses! Either throw first, or let us be the first to throw

20:66.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ أَلۡقُواْۖ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمۡ وَعِصِيُّهُمۡ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيۡهِ مِن سِحۡرِهِمۡ أَنَّهَا تَسۡعَىٰ
20:66.en: He said: Nay, do ye throw! Then lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they ran

20:67.en: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind

20:68.ar: قُلۡنَا لَا تَخَفۡ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ
20:68.en: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher

20:69.ar: وَأَلۡقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلۡقَفۡ مَا صَنَعُوٓاْۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيۡدُ سَٰحِرࣲۖ وَلَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيۡثُ أَتَىٰ
20:69.en: Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard's artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain

20:70.ar: فَأُلۡقِيَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدࣰ ا قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
20:70.en: Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate, crying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses

20:71.ar: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمۡ لَهُۥ قَبۡلَ أَنۡ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحۡرَۖ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفࣲ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمۡ فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخۡلِ وَلَتَعۡلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابࣰ ا وَأَبۡقَىٰ
20:71.en: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he is your chief who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment

20:72.ar: قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَاۖ فَٱقۡضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍۖ إِنَّمَا تَقۡضِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ
20:72.en: They said: We choose thee not above the clear proofs that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us. So decree what thou wilt decree. Thou wilt end for us only this life of the world

20:73.ar: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغۡفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكۡرَهۡتَنَا عَلَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحۡرِۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓ
20:73.en: Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic unto which thou didst force us. Allah is better and more lasting

20:74.ar: إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأۡتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجۡرِمࣰ ا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحۡيَىٰ
20:74.en: Lo! whoso cometh guilty unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die nor live

20:75.ar: وَمَن يَأۡتِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا قَدۡ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلۡعُلَىٰ
20:75.en: But whoso cometh unto Him a believer, having done good works, for such are the high stations

20:76.ar: جَنَّٰتُ عَدۡنࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
20:76.en: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth

20:77.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَسۡرِ بِعِبَادِي فَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُمۡ طَرِيقࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ يَبَسࣰ ا لَّا تَخَٰفُ دَرَكࣰ ا وَلَا تَخۡشَىٰ
20:77.en: And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken, neither being afraid (of the sea)

20:78.ar: فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمۡ
20:78.en: Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea

20:79.en: And Pharaoh led his folk astray, he did not guide them

20:80.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدۡ أَنجَيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ عَدُوِّكُمۡ وَوَٰعَدۡنَٰكُمۡ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنَ وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰ
20:80.en: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and we made a covenant with you on the holy mountain's side, and sent down on you the manna and the quails

20:81.ar: كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَلَا تَطۡغَوۡاْ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَضَبِيۖ وَمَن يَحۡلِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدۡ هَوَىٰ
20:81.en: (Saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you: and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed

20:82.ar: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارࣱ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ
20:82.en: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright

20:83.en: And (it was said): What hath made thee hasten from thy folk, O Moses

20:84.ar: قَالَ هُمۡ أُوْلَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِي وَعَجِلۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ رَبِّ لِتَرۡضَىٰ
20:84.en: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased

20:85.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَوۡمَكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:85.en: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As-Samiri hath misled them

20:86.ar: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَمۡ يَعِدۡكُمۡ رَبُّكُمۡ وَعۡدًا حَسَنًاۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡعَهۡدُ أَمۡ أَرَدتُّمۡ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَضَبࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُم مَّوۡعِدِي
20:86.en: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me

20:87.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَخۡلَفۡنَا مَوۡعِدَكَ بِمَلۡكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلۡنَآ أَوۡزَارࣰ ا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ فَقَذَفۡنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلۡقَى ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:87.en: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed

20:88.ar: فَأَخۡرَجَ لَهُمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارࣱ فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِيَ
20:88.en: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten

20:89.ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوۡنَ أَلَّا يَرۡجِعُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا وَلَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا نَفۡعࣰ ا
20:89.en: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use

20:90.ar: وَلَقَدۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبۡلُ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوٓاْ أَمۡرِي
20:90.en: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order

20:91.ar: قَالُواْ لَن نَّبۡرَحَ عَلَيۡهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرۡجِعَ إِلَيۡنَا مُوسَىٰ
20:91.en: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us

20:92.ar: قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذۡ رَأَيۡتَهُمۡ ضَلُّوٓاْ
20:92.en: He (Moses) said: O Aaron! What held thee back when thou didst see them gone astray

20:93.en: That thou followedst me not? Hast thou then disobeyed my order

20:94.ar: قَالَ يَبۡنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأۡخُذۡ بِلِحۡيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأۡسِيٓۖ إِنِّي خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقۡتَ بَيۡنَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمۡ تَرۡقُبۡ قَوۡلِي
20:94.en: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word

20:95.en: (Moses) said: And what hast thou to say, O Samiri

20:96.ar: قَالَ بَصُرۡتُ بِمَا لَمۡ يَبۡصُرُواْ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضۡتُ قَبۡضَةࣰ مِّنۡ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذۡتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتۡ لِي نَفۡسِي
20:96.en: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me

20:97.ar: قَالَ فَٱذۡهَبۡ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَۖ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوۡعِدࣰ ا لَّن تُخۡلَفَهُۥۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِي ظَلۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ عَاكِفࣰ اۖ لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ نَسۡفًا
20:97.en: (Moses) said: Then go! and lo! in this life it is for thee to say: Touch me not! and lo! there is for thee a tryst thou canst not break. Now look upon thy god of which thou hast remained a votary. Verily we will burn it and will scatter its dust over the sea

20:98.ar: إِنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عِلۡمࣰ ا
20:98.en: Your Allah is only Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah. He embraceth all things in His knowledge

20:99.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدۡ سَبَقَۚ وَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكۡرࣰ ا
20:99.en: Thus relate We unto thee (Muhammad) some tidings of that which happened of old, and We have given thee from Our presence a reminder

20:100.ar: مَّنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَنۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحۡمِلُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وِزۡرًا
20:100.en: Whoso turneth away from it, he verily will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection

20:101.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهِۖ وَسَآءَ لَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ حِمۡلࣰ ا
20:101.en: Abiding under it - an evil burden for them on the Day of Resurrection

20:102.ar: يَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِۚ وَنَحۡشُرُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ زُرۡقࣰ ا
20:102.en: The day when the Trumpet is blown. On that day we assemble the guilty white-eyed (with terror)

20:103.ar: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا عَشۡرࣰ ا
20:103.en: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days)

20:104.ar: نَّحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذۡ يَقُولُ أَمۡثَلُهُمۡ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا يَوۡمࣰ ا
20:104.en: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day

20:105.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡجِبَالِ فَقُلۡ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسۡفࣰ ا
20:105.en: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust

20:106.en: And leave it as an empty plain

20:107.ar: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجࣰ ا وَلَآ أَمۡتࣰ ا
20:107.en: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness

20:108.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلۡأَصۡوَاتُ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا هَمۡسࣰ ا
20:108.en: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur

20:109.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنۡ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا
20:109.en: On that day no intercession availeth save (that of) him unto whom the Beneficent hath given leave and whose word He accepteth

20:110.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣰ ا
20:110.en: He knoweth (all) that is before them and (all) that is behind them, while they cannot compass it in knowledge

20:111.ar: ۞وَعَنَتِ ٱلۡوُجُوهُ لِلۡحَيِّ ٱلۡقَيُّومِۖ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنۡ حَمَلَ ظُلۡمࣰ ا
20:111.en: And faces humble themselves before the Living, the Eternal. And he who beareth (a burden of) wrongdoing is indeed a failure (on that day)

20:112.ar: وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلۡمࣰ ا وَلَا هَضۡمࣰ ا
20:112.en: And he who hath done some good works, being a believer, he feareth not injustice nor begrudging (of his wage)

20:113.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ قُرۡءَانًا عَرَبِيࣰّ ا وَصَرَّفۡنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ أَوۡ يُحۡدِثُ لَهُمۡ ذِكۡرࣰ ا
20:113.en: Thus we have revealed it as a Lecture in Arabic, and have displayed therein certain threats, that peradventure they may keep from evil or that it may cause them to take heed

20:114.ar: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡحَقُّۗ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يُقۡضَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهُۥۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدۡنِي عِلۡمࣰ ا
20:114.en: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge

20:115.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُۥ عَزۡمࣰ ا
20:115.en: And verily We made a covenant of old with Adam, but he forgot, and We found no constancy in him

20:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
20:116.en: And when We said unto the angels: Fall prostrate before Adam, they fell prostrate (all) save Iblis; he refused

20:117.ar: فَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوࣱّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوۡجِكَ فَلَا يُخۡرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ فَتَشۡقَىٰٓ
20:117.en: Therefor we said: O Adam! This is an enemy unto thee and unto thy wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden so that thou come to toil

20:118.ar: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ
20:118.en: It is (vouchsafed) unto thee that thou hungerest not therein nor art naked

20:119.ar: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظۡمَؤُاْ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضۡحَىٰ
20:119.en: And that thou thirstest not therein nor art exposed to the sun's heat

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away

20:121.ar: فَأَكَلَا مِنۡهَا فَبَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ
20:121.en: Then they twain ate thereof, so that their shame became apparent unto them, and they began to hide by heaping on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so went astray

20:122.ar: ثُمَّ ٱجۡتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ وَهَدَىٰ
20:122.en: Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him, and guided him

20:123.ar: قَالَ ٱهۡبِطَا مِنۡهَا جَمِيعَۢاۖ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشۡقَىٰ
20:123.en: He said: Go down hence, both of you, one of you a foe unto the other. But when there come unto you from Me a guidance, then whoso followeth My guidance, he will not go astray nor come to grief

20:124.ar: وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةࣰ ضَنكࣰ ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
20:124.en: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection

20:125.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرۡتَنِيٓ أَعۡمَىٰ وَقَدۡ كُنتُ بَصِيرࣰ ا
20:125.en: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see

20:126.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتۡكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَاۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُنسَىٰ
20:126.en: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day

20:127.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي مَنۡ أَسۡرَفَ وَلَمۡ يُؤۡمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦۚ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓ
20:127.en: Thus do We reward him who is prodigal and believeth not the revelations of his Lord; and verily the doom of the Hereafter will be sterner and more lasting

20:130.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِهَاۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآيِٕ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرۡضَىٰ
20:130.en: Therefor (O Muhammad), bear with what they say, and celebrate the praise of thy Lord ere the rising of the sun and ere the going down thereof. And glorify Him some hours of the night and at the two ends of the day, that thou mayst find acceptance

20:131.ar: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيۡنَيۡكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعۡنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ زَهۡرَةَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لِنَفۡتِنَهُمۡ فِيهِۚ وَرِزۡقُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰ
20:131.en: And strain not thine eyes toward that which We cause some wedded pairs among them to enjoy, the flower of the life of the world, that We may try them thereby. The provision of thy Lord is better and more lasting

20:132.ar: وَأۡمُرۡ أَهۡلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ عَلَيۡهَاۖ لَا نَسۡـَٔلُكَ رِزۡقࣰ اۖ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكَۗ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰ
20:132.en: And enjoin upon thy people worship, and be constant therein. We ask not of thee a provision: We provided for thee. And the sequel is for righteousness

sRCbUqG_Tew.speaker: adnan
sRCbUqG_Tew.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day series; continues parts 1 and 2 of the same juz in his own voice
sRCbUqG_Tew.title: A Juz A Day: 16th Juz, Part 3 - Surah Taha
sRCbUqG_Tew.one_line: A walk through Surah Taha: Musa's call at the fire, his mission to Pharaoh, the golden calf, Adam, and the closing advice to the Prophet.
sRCbUqG_Tew.summary: This third part of the sixteenth juz covers Surah Taha, which he presents as a surah that spends most of its length on the story of Musa from the moment revelation begins. He opens with the reassurance that the Quran was not sent to cause distress, then follows Musa at the fire: Allah, established on His throne and not contained by the world, speaks to him, sets out the etiquette of the sacred valley, tells him he was chosen for the good in him, and gives the core message. He stresses that prayer exists for the remembrance of Allah, so a prayer that does not bring Allah to mind misses its mark. He dwells on Musa's dua for an open heart, an easy task, a loosened tongue and his brother's help, on the love with which Allah raised Musa, on speaking gently even to a tyrant, and on Musa's very human fear before the magicians. Harun's restraint with the calf worshippers is read as wisdom to avoid splitting the people. The closing passages turn to the Day of Judgment, the shortness of worldly life, the miserable life of those who turn from the reminder, and the command to be patient, glorify Allah, keep praying and not crave what others enjoy.

outline.heading: Opening
The Quran was not sent to cause distress
outline.gist: The surah opens by describing the Quran as a reminder from the Creator of the heavens and earth who knows the secret and what is even more hidden.

outline.heading: A surah devoted to the story of Musa
outline.gist: He notes that verses 9 to 99 tell Musa's story in unusual detail, starting from the moment he receives revelation.

outline.heading: Called from the fire in the sacred valley
outline.gist: Musa sees a fire and is addressed by his Lord; Allah is established on His throne yet speaks to him from the fire, tells him to remove his sandals and that he has been chosen.

outline.heading: Prayer for remembrance and the hidden Hour
outline.gist: The purpose of salah is to remember Allah and carry that into life; the Hour is kept hidden so each soul is rewarded for its effort, and desires must not distract from it.

outline.heading: The staff becomes a serpent and the shining hand
outline.gist: Allah asks about the staff He already knows, to show Musa that what he thinks he knows will become a sign; then the hand comes out white, and he is sent to Pharaoh.

outline.heading: Musa's dua for an open heart and a helper
outline.gist: Musa asks for an uplifted heart, an easy task, a loosened tongue and his brother Harun as support, so they can glorify Allah together; he notes teachers open lessons with this dua.

outline.heading: Favours from before: the basket, the sister, the escape
outline.gist: Allah recounts how He saved the infant Musa, returned him to his mother, saved him after the killing, and raised him under His care and love for His service.

outline.heading: Go with My signs and speak gently
outline.gist: Musa and Harun are told to hold to remembrance as things get hard and to speak gently to a tyrant in the hope that he takes heed.

outline.heading: Facing Pharaoh: who is your Lord?
outline.gist: Allah reassures them He is with them; before Pharaoh they demand freedom for the Israelites and describe their Lord as the One who gave everything its form and guided it.

outline.heading: The contest and Musa's human fear
outline.gist: The appointment is set on the festival day so all can witness; Musa feels fear facing a cheering crowd, and Allah tells him to cast the staff because their trick cannot succeed.

outline.heading: The magicians believe and face Pharaoh's threat
outline.gist: The magicians prostrate and accept faith at once despite the threat of crucifixion; Allah contrasts hell for the evildoer with the gardens for those who purify themselves.

outline.heading: The exodus and the blessings on the Israelites
outline.gist: Pharaoh's people drown and the Israelites are reminded of the appointment at the mount, the manna and quails, and the warning not to transgress.

outline.heading: Hastening to the meeting and the golden calf
outline.gist: Musa comes early to meet his Lord, a sign that what matters is met on time; meanwhile the Samiri makes a lowing calf from the people's gold.

outline.heading: Harun's restraint to avoid dividing the people
outline.gist: Harun explains he held back so as not to split the Israelites into warring groups; the Samiri is cast out and the idol destroyed to show it is falsehood.

outline.heading: The Day of Judgment and the shortness of this life
outline.gist: People will guess they stayed ten days or one; voices will be hushed and only permitted intercession will help, so prepare and do not be consumed by this life.

outline.heading: An Arabic Quran and 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge'
outline.gist: The warnings are varied so people may be mindful, and the Prophet is told not to rush the revelation and to ask for more knowledge.

outline.heading: Adam, guidance, and the blindness of turning away
outline.gist: Whoever follows guidance will not go astray or suffer; whoever turns away has a miserable life and is raised blind, having been blind to the revelation.

outline.heading: Patience, glorification, prayer and not craving the world
outline.gist: The surah closes by telling the Prophet to be patient, glorify Allah through the day, keep his family praying and not crave the fleeting splendour given to others.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: The life of Musa from his call at the fire to the golden calf, read for what it teaches about being chosen and carrying a message.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Salah is for remembering Allah; a prayer that does not bring Him to mind misses its purpose.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Musa's dua for an open heart, an easy task, clear speech and a helper, which he recommends before any lesson.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Even a tyrant like Pharaoh is to be addressed gently in the hope he takes heed.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: Harun held back to avoid splitting the people into two warring camps, which he presents as wisdom.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The hushed Day of Judgment and how short worldly life will seem, so prepare rather than be consumed by it.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: Following guidance protects in both lives; turning from the reminder brings a miserable life and blindness on the Day.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Do not let the eyes crave the fleeting splendour others are tested with; what Allah provides in the hereafter is better.

maxims: A salah that does not make us remember Allah misses the mark
When something is important, you are there early for it

stories.who: Musa at the burning bush
stories.point: Allah chose him for the goodness in him and gave him the core message of tawhid and prayer.

stories.who: Musa's infancy in the basket and his sister
stories.point: Allah raised him under His own care and love before ever giving him the mission.

stories.who: Musa and the magicians
stories.point: Even a prophet feels fear facing the crowd and the status quo; Allah's support outweighs the spectacle of falsehood.

stories.who: Harun and the golden calf
stories.point: He held back to prevent division, a reasoned choice rather than weakness.

stories.who: Adam and Satan sent down
stories.point: Guidance will come; whoever follows it is safe and whoever turns away is blind on the Day.

takeaways: Let your prayer actually bring Allah to mind and carry that remembrance into the rest of the day
Make Musa's dua for an open heart and clear speech before teaching or hard tasks
Speak gently even to those who oppose you
Be early and on time for what matters to Allah
Be patient with hurtful words, keep praying and do not crave what others have in this world

20:85.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَوۡمَكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:85.en: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As-Samiri hath misled them

20:86.ar: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَمۡ يَعِدۡكُمۡ رَبُّكُمۡ وَعۡدًا حَسَنًاۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡعَهۡدُ أَمۡ أَرَدتُّمۡ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَضَبࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُم مَّوۡعِدِي
20:86.en: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me

20:87.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَخۡلَفۡنَا مَوۡعِدَكَ بِمَلۡكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلۡنَآ أَوۡزَارࣰ ا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ فَقَذَفۡنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلۡقَى ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:87.en: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed

20:88.ar: فَأَخۡرَجَ لَهُمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارࣱ فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِيَ
20:88.en: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten

20:89.ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوۡنَ أَلَّا يَرۡجِعُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا وَلَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا نَفۡعࣰ ا
20:89.en: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use

20:90.ar: وَلَقَدۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبۡلُ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوٓاْ أَمۡرِي
20:90.en: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order

20:91.ar: قَالُواْ لَن نَّبۡرَحَ عَلَيۡهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرۡجِعَ إِلَيۡنَا مُوسَىٰ
20:91.en: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us

21:51.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ رُشۡدَهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
21:51.en: And We verily gave Abraham of old his proper course, and We were Aware of him

21:52.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
21:52.en: When he said unto his father and his folk: What are these images unto which ye pay devotion

21:53.en: They said: We found our fathers worshippers of them

21:54.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُمۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
21:54.en: He said: Verily ye and your fathers were in plain error

21:55.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَجِئۡتَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ أَمۡ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
21:55.en: They said: Bringest thou unto us the truth, or art thou some jester

21:56.ar: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمۡ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
21:56.en: He said: Nay, but your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them; and I am of those who testify unto that

21:57.ar: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصۡنَٰمَكُم بَعۡدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدۡبِرِينَ
21:57.en: And, by Allah, I shall circumvent your idols after ye have gone away and turned your backs

21:58.ar: فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ يَرۡجِعُونَ
21:58.en: Then he reduced them to fragments, all save the chief of them, that haply they might have recourse to it

21:59.ar: قَالُواْ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
21:59.en: They said: Who hath done this to our gods? Surely it must be some evil-doer

21:60.ar: قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا فَتࣰ ى يَذۡكُرُهُمۡ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ
21:60.en: They said: We heard a youth make mention of them, who is called Abraham

21:61.ar: قَالُواْ فَأۡتُواْ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡهَدُونَ
21:61.en: They said: Then bring him (hither) before the people's eyes that they may testify

21:62.ar: قَالُوٓاْ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلۡتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ
21:62.en: They said: Is it thou who hast done this to our gods, O Abraham

21:63.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمۡ هَٰذَا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُمۡ إِن كَانُواْ يَنطِقُونَ
21:63.en: He said: But this, their chief hath done it. So question them, if they can speak

21:64.ar: فَرَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّكُمۡ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
21:64.en: Then gathered they apart and said: Lo! ye yourselves are the wrong-doers

21:65.ar: ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمۡ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
21:65.en: And they were utterly confounded, and they said: Well thou knowest that these speak not

21:66.ar: قَالَ أَفَتَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ
21:66.en: He said: Worship ye then instead of Allah that which cannot profit you at all, nor harm you

21:67.ar: أُفࣲّ لَّكُمۡ وَلِمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
21:67.en: Fie on you and all that ye worship instead of Allah! Have ye then no sense

21:68.ar: قَالُواْ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓاْ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ فَٰعِلِينَ
21:68.en: They cried: Burn him and stand by your gods, if ye will be doing

22:11.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
22:11.en: And among mankind is he who worshippeth Allah upon a narrow marge so that if good befalleth him he is content therewith, but if a trial befalleth him, he falleth away utterly. He loseth both the world and the Hereafter. That is the sheer loss

22:12.ar: يَدۡعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُۥ وَمَا لَا يَنفَعُهُۥۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَٰلُ ٱلۡبَعِيدُ
22:12.en: He calleth, beside Allah, unto that which hurteth him not nor benefiteth him. That is the far error

22:13.ar: يَدۡعُواْ لَمَن ضَرُّهُۥٓ أَقۡرَبُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِۦۚ لَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَلَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡعَشِيرُ
22:13.en: He calleth unto him whose harm is nearer than his benefit; verily an evil patron and verily an evil friend

7:138.ar: وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ يَعۡكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصۡنَامࣲ لَّهُمۡۚ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجۡعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهࣰ ا كَمَا لَهُمۡ ءَالِهَةࣱۚ قَالَ إِنَّكُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ تَجۡهَلُونَ
7:138.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came unto a people who were given up to idols which they had. They said: O Moses! Make for us a god even as they have gods. He said: Lo! ye are a folk who know not

37:89.en: Then said: Lo! I feel sick

17:81.ar: وَقُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقࣰ ا
17:81.en: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish

t0OcFedj33s.speaker: adnan
t0OcFedj33s.speaker_note: Sh. Adnan's Ramadan halqa series; speaks of his own years of study and his minbar in the community
t0OcFedj33s.title: Exposing Irrationality (Ramadan 2026, Night 16: Quranic Themes 2)
t0OcFedj33s.one_line: How the Quran exposes irrational beliefs, from the golden calf and Ibrahim's idols to conditional worship, and why ideas must change at the root.
t0OcFedj33s.summary: He begins with how baseless ideas spread from one loud voice into unquestioned norms. Truth wins in the end, but slowly. Superstitions, astrology and belief in jinn steering people's minds have no evidence, yet parents still take children to exorcists, and correcting such irrationalities is the minbar's job, which only works if people question what they inherited. The Quran exposes irrationality with simple questions. Bani Israel, after every miracle and the parted sea, worshipped a lowing golden calf, and the Quran asks whether they could not see it gives no answer and has no power to harm or benefit; he compares people pleading at shrines where no one is buried. Centuries of decline left Muslims with defeated ideas and severe literalism, where a teenager with one hadith from YouTube lectures a scholar. Ibrahim kept his reason as a child, broke the idols and told his people to ask the largest one; they saw the truth for a moment and then burned him anyway. The Prophet never broke the Ka'bah's idols in Mecca; he spent twenty years changing minds until the idols fell when he pointed at them. Muslims must first fix their own false certainties, which drive youth away. Finally, worshipping Allah only when things go well loses both this world and the next.

outline.heading: How baseless ideas become norms
outline.gist: One popular or powerful voice backed by key people can turn an absurd, evidence-free idea into public opinion and then an unquestioned maxim.

outline.heading: Truth prevails, but slowly
outline.gist: Muslims believe the stronger idea, the truth, eventually wins and falsehood is discarded, but it does not happen automatically.

outline.heading: Superstitions and astrology
outline.gist: Not walking under ladders and believing planets decide your fate are baseless ideas that have floated for centuries and are hard to remove.

outline.heading: Jinn possession and exorcisms
outline.gist: Muslims have superstitions too, such as a jinn sitting in the brain steering a person; there is no evidence for it, yet after he explains this people still take their children to exorcists. Correcting such ideas is the masjid's main job.

outline.heading: Critical thinking comes first
outline.gist: Unless people are willing to question themselves and what they inherited from parents and society, there is little hope of changing minds; the Quran exposes irrationality elegantly.

outline.heading: Miracle after miracle for a hard-headed people
outline.gist: Bani Israel saw the staff, the shining hand and the plagues that struck only the Egyptians, then crossed the sea and watched Pharaoh drown.

outline.heading: Their feet still wet from the sea
outline.gist: Musa leaves for a few days and is told the Samiri has misled them; he returns angry and sad, asking whether the promise seemed too long in coming.

outline.heading: The golden calf that made a sound
outline.gist: The Samiri made a lowing golden calf and they called it Musa's god, forgetting nine miracles; raised among Egyptian pagans, they wanted a shiny god like everyone else.

outline.heading: 'Do they not see it cannot answer them?'
outline.gist: The Quran exposes the calf simply: it cannot speak, harm or benefit them, and has no power over anything.

outline.heading: A visible god should at least do what you can
outline.gist: If you worship something present before you, it should at least communicate and have power you lack; the calf does nothing for them.

outline.heading: Shrines with no one buried in them
outline.gist: People rub themselves on graves and leave money asking for marriages and houses, even at shrines where no one is buried, because ideas are so hard to dislodge.

outline.heading: The Prophet changed ideas first
outline.gist: His miracle was changing ideas before anything else; centuries of decline have left Muslims with ideas that belong to a defeated population, not to Islam.

outline.heading: Literalism comes from intellectual defeat
outline.gist: Severe literalism thrives where people are intellectually bankrupt; a youth who reads one hadith online lectures scholars, which no other discipline would tolerate.

outline.heading: Start with the simple irrationalities
outline.gist: He once argued with a fourteen-year-old over a term he studied for twenty-five years without being permitted to use; the Quran's method is to begin with basic questions.

outline.heading: Harun explained, but they waited for Musa
outline.gist: Harun, the scholar, explained everything, but they would only listen to Musa, whom they feared.

outline.heading: Ibrahim held on to his reason
outline.gist: As a child Ibrahim refused the inherited lies about idols; Allah helped him, since children usually cannot withstand such a flood of ideas.

outline.heading: Staying behind from the festival
outline.gist: His arguments only annoyed people, so he said he was sick and stayed behind when everyone left for their celebration.

outline.heading: Breaking the idols
outline.gist: He told the idols to eat and speak, smashed them and left the axe in the hand of the largest; the people returned and summoned him.

outline.heading: 'Ask them, if they can speak'
outline.gist: He blamed the biggest idol; for a moment they turned to themselves and admitted they were the wrongdoers.

outline.heading: Turned on their heads
outline.gist: They flipped back, thinking upside down, and said he knew idols cannot speak; he asked why they worship what cannot help or harm them.

outline.heading: Burning the one who 'killed their gods'
outline.gist: They threw him into an enormous fire for killing their gods, an absurd sentence; exposing their irrationality did not change them, and he was driven out.

outline.heading: The Prophet never broke the idols in Mecca
outline.gist: With over 360 idols around the Ka'bah, he never sent anyone to break one; he had learned from Ibrahim and spent twenty years striving to change minds.

outline.heading: Change the idea and the idol falls
outline.gist: At the conquest he recited an ayah and pointed, and the idols fell by themselves; debunking a symbol does not change the root idea.

outline.heading: Breaking symbols creates martyrs
outline.gist: Smashing idols hands their followers propaganda and sympathy; change the mind that gives them meaning and they fade away. Ibrahim, young, exposed the irrationality perfectly, but ideas do not change that way.

outline.heading: First fix our own false certainties
outline.gist: When parents bring him children who have left Islam, they have often been fed misconceptions for so long that nothing he says can reach them.

outline.heading: Stop taking your kids to exorcists
outline.gist: Parents only know the Islam they were told; he has preached against jinn removal for years, yet people still take children to men who beat them to drive a jinn out.

outline.heading: Spread Islam's proper ideas
outline.gist: To spread Islam we must change how we understand the world and ourselves and spread its proper ethics, values and understanding; there is a long way to go.

outline.heading: Worshipping Allah on the edge
outline.gist: Some worship Allah at the edge of a cliff: content when they are healthy and wealthy, and falling away the moment hardship comes.

outline.heading: Losing this world and the next
outline.gist: Turning bitter and leaving the faith in hardship does not improve worldly life and costs the hereafter; then they call on what can neither harm nor help them.

outline.heading: Conditional worship makes no sense
outline.gist: What they call on harms more than it helps; you worship Allah because He is Allah, and worship Him more when you do not get what you want.

outline.heading: A child's tantrum
outline.gist: Abandoning faith over a hardship is like a four-year-old who breaks his toy when told no; persevere so at least your hereafter is safe.

outline.heading: Meet hardship and win both
outline.gist: Even on logic alone, losing both worlds is absurd; facing difficulty with optimism and effort brings contentment now and reward later.

themes.label: Conspiracy thinking and critical thinking
themes.note: Baseless ideas spread into unquestioned norms; superstitions and astrology survive because people do not question what they inherit.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Belief in jinn controlling the mind and the practice of exorcism have no basis in the deen.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Musa's people worship a golden calf after every miracle, and the Quran exposes the irrationality with a simple question.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: What cannot speak, harm or benefit cannot be worshipped, whether a calf or an empty shrine.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Severe literalism and arguing from a single hadith reflect intellectual defeat and disregard for the depth of Islamic scholarship.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim keeps his reason, breaks the idols and exposes his people, who burn him anyway.

themes.label: Reform (islah)
themes.note: The Prophet changed ideas at the root rather than attacking symbols; Muslims must first correct their own false certainties.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people leave Islam after being fed misconceptions presented as the deen.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Conditional faith that collapses in hardship loses both worlds; perseverance wins both.

Ibrahim says he is sick so he can stay behind from the festival.

hadith.gist: At the conquest of Mecca the Prophet, on his mount, recited an ayah and pointed at each idol around the Ka'bah, and it fell over by itself.

takeaways: Question inherited beliefs and practise critical thinking.
Stop taking children to exorcists and jinn removers.
