17:1.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَسۡرَىٰ بِعَبۡدِهِۦ لَيۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡأَقۡصَا ٱلَّذِي بَٰرَكۡنَا حَوۡلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
17:1.en: Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed, that We might show him of Our tokens! Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

17:2.ar: وَءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ هُدࣰ ى لِّبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلࣰ ا
17:2.en: We gave unto Moses the Scripture, and We appointed it a guidance for the children of Israel, saying: Choose no guardian beside Me

17:3.ar: ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنۡ حَمَلۡنَا مَعَ نُوحٍۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَبۡدࣰ ا شَكُورࣰ ا
17:3.en: (They were) the seed of those whom We carried (in the ship) along with Noah. Lo! he was a grateful slave

17:4.ar: وَقَضَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَتُفۡسِدُنَّ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَّتَيۡنِ وَلَتَعۡلُنَّ عُلُوࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:4.en: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture: Ye verily will work corruption in the earth twice, and ye will become great tyrants

17:5.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ أُولَىٰهُمَا بَعَثۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ عِبَادࣰ ا لَّنَآ أُوْلِي بَأۡسࣲ شَدِيدࣲ فَجَاسُواْ خِلَٰلَ ٱلدِّيَارِۚ وَكَانَ وَعۡدࣰ ا مَّفۡعُولࣰ ا
17:5.en: So when the time for the first of the two came, We roused against you slaves of Ours of great might who ravaged (your) country, and it was a threat performed

17:6.ar: ثُمَّ رَدَدۡنَا لَكُمُ ٱلۡكَرَّةَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَأَمۡدَدۡنَٰكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أَكۡثَرَ نَفِيرًا
17:6.en: Then we gave you once again your turn against them, and We aided you with wealth and children and made you more in soldiery

17:7.ar: إِنۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡۖ وَإِنۡ أَسَأۡتُمۡ فَلَهَاۚ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لِيَسُـُٔواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ وَلِيَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوۡاْ تَتۡبِيرًا
17:7.en: (Saying): If ye do good, ye do good for your own souls, and if ye do evil, it is for them (in like manner). So, when the time for the second (of the judgments) came (We roused against you others of Our slaves) to ravage you, and to enter the Temple even as they entered it the first time, and to lay waste all that they conquered with an utter wasting

17:8.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يَرۡحَمَكُمۡۚ وَإِنۡ عُدتُّمۡ عُدۡنَاۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ حَصِيرًا
17:8.en: It may be that your Lord will have mercy on you, but if ye repeat (the crime) We shall repeat (the punishment), and We have appointed hell a dungeon for the disbelievers

17:9.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ يَهۡدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقۡوَمُ وَيُبَشِّرُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:9.en: Lo! this Qur'an guideth unto that which is straightest, and giveth tidings unto the believers who do good works that theirs will be a great reward

17:10.ar: وَأَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
17:10.en: And that those who believe not in the Hereafter, for them We have prepared a painful doom

17:11.ar: وَيَدۡعُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ بِٱلشَّرِّ دُعَآءَهُۥ بِٱلۡخَيۡرِۖ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ عَجُولࣰ ا
17:11.en: Man prayeth for evil as he prayeth for good; for man was ever hasty

17:12.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ ءَايَتَيۡنِۖ فَمَحَوۡنَآ ءَايَةَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَجَعَلۡنَآ ءَايَةَ ٱلنَّهَارِ مُبۡصِرَةࣰ لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَلِتَعۡلَمُواْ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلۡحِسَابَۚ وَكُلَّ شَيۡءࣲ فَصَّلۡنَٰهُ تَفۡصِيلࣰ ا
17:12.en: And We appoint the night and the day two portents. Then We make dark the portent of the night, and We make the portent of the day sight-giving, that ye may seek bounty from your Lord, and that ye may know the computation of the years, and the reckoning; and everything have We expounded with a clear expounding

17:13.ar: وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلۡزَمۡنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِي عُنُقِهِۦۖ وَنُخۡرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا يَلۡقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
17:13.en: And every man's augury have We fastened to his own neck, and We shall bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

17:15.ar: مَّنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهۡتَدِي لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡهَاۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةࣱ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبۡعَثَ رَسُولࣰ ا
17:15.en: Whosoever goeth right, it is only for (the good of) his own soul that he goeth right, and whosoever erreth, erreth only to its hurt. No laden soul can bear another's load, We never punish until we have sent a messenger

17:16.ar: وَإِذَآ أَرَدۡنَآ أَن نُّهۡلِكَ قَرۡيَةً أَمَرۡنَا مُتۡرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُواْ فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فَدَمَّرۡنَٰهَا تَدۡمِيرࣰ ا
17:16.en: And when We would destroy a township We send commandment to its folk who live at ease, and afterward they commit abomination therein, and so the Word (of doom) hath effect for it, and we annihilate it with complete annihilation

17:17.ar: وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ نُوحࣲۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرَۢا بَصِيرࣰ ا
17:17.en: How many generations have We destroyed since Noah! And Allah sufficeth as Knower and Beholder of the sins of His slaves

17:18.ar: مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلۡعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلۡنَا لَهُۥ فِيهَا مَا نَشَآءُ لِمَن نُّرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ يَصۡلَىٰهَا مَذۡمُومࣰ ا مَّدۡحُورࣰ ا
17:18.en: Whoso desireth that (life) which hasteneth away, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We please. And afterward We have appointed for him hell; he will endure the heat thereof, condemned, rejected

17:19.ar: وَمَنۡ أَرَادَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعۡيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ سَعۡيُهُم مَّشۡكُورࣰ ا
17:19.en: And whoso desireth the Hereafter and striveth for it with the effort necessary, being a believer; for such, their effort findeth favour (with their Lord)

17:20.ar: كُلࣰّ ا نُّمِدُّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مِنۡ عَطَآءِ رَبِّكَۚ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَآءُ رَبِّكَ مَحۡظُورًا
17:20.en: Each do We supply, both these and those, from the bounty of thy Lord. And the bounty of thy Lord can never be walled up

17:21.ar: ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ فَضَّلۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲۚ وَلَلۡأٓخِرَةُ أَكۡبَرُ دَرَجَٰتࣲ وَأَكۡبَرُ تَفۡضِيلࣰ ا
17:21.en: See how We prefer one of them above another, and verily the Hereafter will be greater in degrees and greater in preferment

17:22.ar: لَّا تَجۡعَلۡ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقۡعُدَ مَذۡمُومࣰ ا مَّخۡذُولࣰ ا
17:22.en: Set not up with Allah any other god (O man) lest thou sit down reproved, forsaken

17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

17:24.ar: وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرࣰ ا
17:24.en: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little

17:25.ar: رَّبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمۡۚ إِن تَكُونُواْ صَٰلِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِلۡأَوَّٰبِينَ غَفُورࣰ ا
17:25.en: Your Lord is Best Aware of what is in your minds. If ye are righteous, then lo! He was ever Forgiving unto those who turn (unto Him)

17:26.ar: وَءَاتِ ذَا ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ حَقَّهُۥ وَٱلۡمِسۡكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرۡ تَبۡذِيرًا
17:26.en: Give the kinsman his due, and the needy, and the wayfarer, and squander not (thy wealth) in wantonness

17:27.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوٓاْ إِخۡوَٰنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِرَبِّهِۦ كَفُورࣰ ا
17:27.en: Lo! the squanderers were ever brothers of the devils, and the devil was ever an ingrate to his Lord

17:28.ar: وَإِمَّا تُعۡرِضَنَّ عَنۡهُمُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرۡجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّيۡسُورࣰ ا
17:28.en: But if thou turn away from them, seeking mercy from thy Lord, for which thou hopest, then speak unto them a reasonable word

17:29.ar: وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ يَدَكَ مَغۡلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبۡسُطۡهَا كُلَّ ٱلۡبَسۡطِ فَتَقۡعُدَ مَلُومࣰ ا مَّحۡسُورًا
17:29.en: And let not thy hand be chained to thy neck nor open it with a complete opening, lest thou sit down rebuked, denuded

17:30.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرَۢا بَصِيرࣰ ا
17:30.en: Lo! thy Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will, and straiteneth (it for whom He will). Lo, He was ever Knower, Seer of His slaves

17:31.ar: وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُمۡ خَشۡيَةَ إِمۡلَٰقࣲۖ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُهُمۡ وَإِيَّاكُمۡۚ إِنَّ قَتۡلَهُمۡ كَانَ خِطۡـࣰٔ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:31.en: Slay not your children, fearing a fall to poverty, We shall provide for them and for you. Lo! the slaying of them is great sin

17:32.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةࣰ وَسَآءَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:32.en: And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination and an evil way

17:33.ar: وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظۡلُومࣰ ا فَقَدۡ جَعَلۡنَا لِوَلِيِّهِۦ سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَلَا يُسۡرِف فِّي ٱلۡقَتۡلِۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مَنصُورࣰ ا
17:33.en: And slay not the life which Allah hath forbidden save with right. Whoso is slain wrongfully, We have given power unto his heir, but let him not commit excess in slaying. Lo! he will be helped

17:34.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلۡيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥۚ وَأَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعَهۡدِۖ إِنَّ ٱلۡعَهۡدَ كَانَ مَسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
17:34.en: Come not near the wealth of the orphan save with that which is better till he come to strength; and keep the covenant. Lo! of the covenant it will be asked

17:35.ar: وَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ إِذَا كِلۡتُمۡ وَزِنُواْ بِٱلۡقِسۡطَاسِ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمِۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَحۡسَنُ تَأۡوِيلࣰ ا
17:35.en: Fill the measure when ye measure, and weigh with a right balance; that is meet, and better in the end

17:36.ar: وَلَا تَقۡفُ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡبَصَرَ وَٱلۡفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنۡهُ مَسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
17:36.en: (O man), follow not that whereof thou hast no knowledge. Lo! the hearing and the sight and the heart - of each of these it will be asked

17:37.ar: وَلَا تَمۡشِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَحًاۖ إِنَّكَ لَن تَخۡرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَن تَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡجِبَالَ طُولࣰ ا
17:37.en: And walk not in the earth exultant. Lo! thou canst not rend the earth, nor canst thou stretch to the height of the hills

17:38.ar: كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ كَانَ سَيِّئُهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّكَ مَكۡرُوهࣰ ا
17:38.en: The evil of all that is hateful in the sight of thy Lord

17:39.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مِمَّآ أَوۡحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةِۗ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتُلۡقَىٰ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومࣰ ا مَّدۡحُورًا
17:39.en: This is (part) of that wisdom wherewith thy Lord hath inspired thee (O Muhammad). And set not up with Allah any other god, lest thou be cast into hell, reproved, abandoned

17:40.ar: أَفَأَصۡفَىٰكُمۡ رَبُّكُم بِٱلۡبَنِينَ وَٱتَّخَذَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنَٰثًاۚ إِنَّكُمۡ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوۡلًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
17:40.en: Hath your Lord then distinguished you (O men of Makka) by giving you sons, and hath chosen for Himself females from among the angels? Lo! verily ye speak an awful word

17:41.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا فِي هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ لِيَذَّكَّرُواْ وَمَا يَزِيدُهُمۡ إِلَّا نُفُورࣰ ا
17:41.en: We verily have displayed (Our warnings) in this Qur'an that they may take heed, but it increaseth them in naught save aversion

17:42.ar: قُل لَّوۡ كَانَ مَعَهُۥٓ ءَالِهَةࣱ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذࣰ ا لَّٱبۡتَغَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِي ٱلۡعَرۡشِ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:42.en: Say (O Muhammad, to the disbelievers): If there were other gods along with Him, as they say, then had they sought a way against the Lord of the Throne

17:43.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:43.en: Glorified is He, and High Exalted above what they say

17:44.ar: تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّۚ وَإِن مِّن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
17:44.en: The seven heavens and the earth and all that is therein praise Him, and there is not a thing but hymneth His praise; but ye understand not their praise. Lo! He is ever Clement, Forgiving

17:45.ar: وَإِذَا قَرَأۡتَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ جَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ حِجَابࣰ ا مَّسۡتُورࣰ ا
17:45.en: And when thou recitest the Qur'an we place between thee and those who believe not in the Hereafter a hidden barrier

17:46.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفۡقَهُوهُ وَفِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَقۡرࣰ اۚ وَإِذَا ذَكَرۡتَ رَبَّكَ فِي ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَحۡدَهُۥ وَلَّوۡاْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَٰرِهِمۡ نُفُورࣰ ا
17:46.en: And We place upon their hearts veils lest they should understand it, and in their ears a deafness; and when thou makest mention of thy Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion

17:47.ar: نَّحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَسۡتَمِعُونَ بِهِۦٓ إِذۡ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِذۡ هُمۡ نَجۡوَىٰٓ إِذۡ يَقُولُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلࣰ ا مَّسۡحُورًا
17:47.en: We are Best Aware of what they wish to hear when they give ear to thee and when they take secret counsel, when the evil-doers say: Ye follow but a man bewitched

17:48.ar: ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ ضَرَبُواْ لَكَ ٱلۡأَمۡثَالَ فَضَلُّواْ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:48.en: See what similitudes they coin for thee, and thus are all astray, and cannot find a road

17:49.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمࣰ ا وَرُفَٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ خَلۡقࣰ ا جَدِيدࣰ ا
17:49.en: And they say: When we are bones and fragments, shall we forsooth, be raised up as a new creation

17:50.en: Say: Be ye stones or iron

17:51.ar: أَوۡ خَلۡقࣰ ا مِّمَّا يَكۡبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمۡۚ فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَن يُعِيدُنَاۖ قُلِ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲۚ فَسَيُنۡغِضُونَ إِلَيۡكَ رُءُوسَهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هُوَۖ قُلۡ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَرِيبࣰ ا
17:51.en: Or some created thing that is yet greater in your thoughts! Then they will say: Who shall bring us back (to life). Say: He Who created you at the first. Then will they shake their heads at thee, and say: When will it be? Say: It will perhaps be soon

17:52.ar: يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ فَتَسۡتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَتَظُنُّونَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:52.en: A day when He will call you and ye will answer with His praise, and ye will think that ye have tarried but a little while

17:53.ar: وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي يَقُولُواْ ٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُۚ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ يَنزَغُ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوࣰّ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
17:53.en: Tell My bondmen to speak that which is kindlier. Lo! the devil soweth discord among them. Lo! the devil is for man an open foe

17:54.ar: رَّبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡۖ إِن يَشَأۡ يَرۡحَمۡكُمۡ أَوۡ إِن يَشَأۡ يُعَذِّبۡكُمۡۚ وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَكِيلࣰ ا
17:54.en: Your Lord is Best Aware of you. If He will, He will have mercy on you, or if He will, He will punish you. We have not sent thee (O Muhammad) as a warden over them

17:55.ar: وَرَبُّكَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَلَقَدۡ فَضَّلۡنَا بَعۡضَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُۥدَ زَبُورࣰ ا
17:55.en: And thy Lord is Best Aware of all who are in the heavens and the earth. And we preferred some of the prophets above others, and unto David We gave the Psalms

17:56.ar: قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَلَا يَمۡلِكُونَ كَشۡفَ ٱلضُّرِّ عَنكُمۡ وَلَا تَحۡوِيلًا
17:56.en: Say: Cry unto those (saints and angels) whom ye assume (to be gods) beside Him, yet they have no power to rid you of misfortune nor to change

17:57.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ يَبۡتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلۡوَسِيلَةَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ وَيَرۡجُونَ رَحۡمَتَهُۥ وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ كَانَ مَحۡذُورࣰ ا
17:57.en: Those unto whom they cry seek the way of approach to their Lord, which of them shall be the nearest; they hope for His mercy and they fear His doom. Lo! the doom of thy Lord is to be shunned

17:58.ar: وَإِن مِّن قَرۡيَةٍ إِلَّا نَحۡنُ مُهۡلِكُوهَا قَبۡلَ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَسۡطُورࣰ ا
17:58.en: There is not a township but We shall destroy it ere the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with dire punishment. That is set forth in the Book (of Our decrees)

17:59.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرۡسِلَ بِٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ إِلَّآ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا ٱلۡأَوَّلُونَۚ وَءَاتَيۡنَا ثَمُودَ ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبۡصِرَةࣰ فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَاۚ وَمَا نُرۡسِلُ بِٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ إِلَّا تَخۡوِيفࣰ ا
17:59.en: Naught hindereth Us from sending portents save that the folk of old denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel - a clear portent save to warn

17:60.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِۚ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلرُّءۡيَا ٱلَّتِيٓ أَرَيۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلۡمَلۡعُونَةَ فِي ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَنُخَوِّفُهُمۡ فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمۡ إِلَّا طُغۡيَٰنࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:60.en: And (it was a warning) when we told thee: Lo! thy Lord encompasseth mankind, and We appointed the sight which We showed thee as an ordeal for mankind, and (likewise) the Accursed Tree in the Qur'an. We warn them, but it increaseth them in naught save gross impiety

17:61.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ قَالَ ءَأَسۡجُدُ لِمَنۡ خَلَقۡتَ طِينࣰ ا
17:61.en: And when We said unto the angels: Fall down prostrate before Adam and they fell prostrate all save Iblis, he said: Shall I fall prostrate before that which Thou hast created of clay

18:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِهِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَلَمۡ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ عِوَجَاۜ
18:1.en: Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed therein any crookedness

18:2.ar: قَيِّمࣰ ا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأۡسࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا مِّن لَّدُنۡهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرًا حَسَنࣰ ا
18:2.en: (But hath made it) straight, to give warning of stern punishment from Him, and to bring unto the believers who do good works the news that theirs will be a fair reward

18:3.en: Wherein they will abide for ever

18:4.ar: وَيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدࣰ ا
18:4.en: And to warn those who say: Allah hath chosen a son

18:5.ar: مَّا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمࣲ وَلَا لِأٓبَآئِهِمۡۚ كَبُرَتۡ كَلِمَةࣰ تَخۡرُجُ مِنۡ أَفۡوَٰهِهِمۡۚ إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبࣰ ا
18:5.en: (A thing) whereof they have no knowledge, nor (had) their fathers, Dreadful is the word that cometh out of their mouths. They speak naught but a lie

18:6.ar: فَلَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعࣱ نَّفۡسَكَ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمۡ إِن لَّمۡ يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا
18:6.en: Yet it may be, if they believe not in this statement, that thou (Muhammad) wilt torment thy soul with grief over their footsteps

18:7.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ زِينَةࣰ لَّهَا لِنَبۡلُوَهُمۡ أَيُّهُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ ا
18:7.en: Lo! We have placed all that is on the earth as an ornament thereof that We may try them: which of them is best in conduct

18:8.ar: وَإِنَّا لَجَٰعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيۡهَا صَعِيدࣰ ا جُرُزًا
18:8.en: And lo! We shall make all that is thereon a barren mound

18:9.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ أَنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡكَهۡفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
18:9.en: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents

18:10.ar: إِذۡ أَوَى ٱلۡفِتۡيَةُ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةࣰ وَهَيِّئۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا رَشَدࣰ ا
18:10.en: When the young men fled for refuge to the Cave and said: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight

18:11.ar: فَضَرَبۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ فِي ٱلۡكَهۡفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدࣰ ا
18:11.en: Then We sealed up their hearing in the Cave for a number of years

18:12.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰهُمۡ لِنَعۡلَمَ أَيُّ ٱلۡحِزۡبَيۡنِ أَحۡصَىٰ لِمَا لَبِثُوٓاْ أَمَدࣰ ا
18:12.en: And afterward We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties would best calculate the time that they had tarried

18:13.ar: نَّحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ نَبَأَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّهُمۡ فِتۡيَةٌ ءَامَنُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ وَزِدۡنَٰهُمۡ هُدࣰ ى
18:13.en: We narrate unto thee their story with truth. Lo! they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance

18:14.ar: وَرَبَطۡنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ إِذۡ قَامُواْ فَقَالُواْ رَبُّنَا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَن نَّدۡعُوَاْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَٰهࣰ اۖ لَّقَدۡ قُلۡنَآ إِذࣰ ا شَطَطًا
18:14.en: And We made firm their hearts when they stood forth and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We cry unto no Allah beside Him, for then should we utter an enormity

18:15.ar: هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمُنَا ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةࣰۖ لَّوۡلَا يَأۡتُونَ عَلَيۡهِم بِسُلۡطَٰنِۭ بَيِّنࣲۖ فَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
18:15.en: These, our people, have chosen (other) gods beside Him though they bring no clear warrant (vouchsafed) to them. And who doth greater wrong than he who inventeth a lie concerning Allah

18:16.ar: وَإِذِ ٱعۡتَزَلۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأۡوُۥٓاْ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ يَنشُرۡ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئۡ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَمۡرِكُم مِّرۡفَقࣰ ا
18:16.en: And when ye withdraw from them and that which they worship except Allah, then seek refuge in the Cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a pillow in your plight

18:17.ar: ۞وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمۡسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٰوَرُ عَن كَهۡفِهِمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقۡرِضُهُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ وَهُمۡ فِي فَجۡوَةࣲ مِّنۡهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۗ مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ وَلِيࣰّ ا مُّرۡشِدࣰ ا
18:17.en: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it rose move away from their cave to the right, and when it set go past them on the left, and they were in the cleft thereof. That was (one) of the portents of Allah. He whom Allah guideth, he indeed is led aright, and he whom He sendeth astray, for him thou wilt not find a guiding friend

18:18.ar: وَتَحۡسَبُهُمۡ أَيۡقَاظࣰ ا وَهُمۡ رُقُودࣱۚ وَنُقَلِّبُهُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِۖ وَكَلۡبُهُم بَٰسِطࣱ ذِرَاعَيۡهِ بِٱلۡوَصِيدِۚ لَوِ ٱطَّلَعۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَوَلَّيۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ فِرَارࣰ ا وَلَمُلِئۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ رُعۡبࣰ ا
18:18.en: And thou wouldst have deemed them waking though they were asleep, and We caused them to turn over to the right and the left, and their dog stretching out his paws on the threshold. If thou hadst observed them closely thou hadst assuredly turned away from them in flight, and hadst been filled with awe of them

18:19.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ بَعَثۡنَٰهُمۡ لِيَتَسَآءَلُواْ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ قَالَ قَآئِلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲۚ قَالُواْ رَبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثۡتُمۡ فَٱبۡعَثُوٓاْ أَحَدَكُم بِوَرِقِكُمۡ هَٰذِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ فَلۡيَنظُرۡ أَيُّهَآ أَزۡكَىٰ طَعَامࣰ ا فَلۡيَأۡتِكُم بِرِزۡقࣲ مِّنۡهُ وَلۡيَتَلَطَّفۡ وَلَا يُشۡعِرَنَّ بِكُمۡ أَحَدًا
18:19.en: And in like manner We awakened them that they might question one another. A speaker from among them said: How long have ye tarried? They said: We have tarried a day or some part of a day, (Others) said: Your Lord best knoweth what ye have tarried. Now send one of you with this your silver coin unto the city, and let him see what food is purest there and bring you a supply thereof. Let him be courteous and let no man know of you

18:20.ar: إِنَّهُمۡ إِن يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ يَرۡجُمُوكُمۡ أَوۡ يُعِيدُوكُمۡ فِي مِلَّتِهِمۡ وَلَن تُفۡلِحُوٓاْ إِذًا أَبَدࣰ ا
18:20.en: For they, if they should come to know of you, will stone you or turn you back to their religion; then ye will never prosper

18:21.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَعۡثَرۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهَآ إِذۡ يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ أَمۡرَهُمۡۖ فَقَالُواْ ٱبۡنُواْ عَلَيۡهِم بُنۡيَٰنࣰ اۖ رَّبُّهُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِهِمۡۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ غَلَبُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِهِمۡ لَنَتَّخِذَنَّ عَلَيۡهِم مَّسۡجِدࣰ ا
18:21.en: And in like manner We disclosed them (to the people of the city) that they might know that the promise of Allah is true, and that, as for the Hour, there is no doubt concerning it. When (the people of the city) disputed of their case among themselves, they said: Build over them a building; their Lord knoweth best concerning them. Those who won their point said: We verily shall build a place of worship over them

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them

18:23.ar: وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَاْيۡءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلࣱ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا
18:23.en: And say not of anything: Lo! I shall do that tomorrow

18:24.ar: إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ وَقُلۡ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَهۡدِيَنِ رَبِّي لِأَقۡرَبَ مِنۡ هَٰذَا رَشَدࣰ ا
18:24.en: Except if Allah will. And remember thy Lord when thou forgettest, and say: It may be that my Lord guideth me unto a nearer way of truth than this

18:25.ar: وَلَبِثُواْ فِي كَهۡفِهِمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مِاْئَةࣲ سِنِينَ وَٱزۡدَادُواْ تِسۡعࣰ ا
18:25.en: And (it is said) they tarried in their Cave three hundred years and add nine

18:26.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُواْۖ لَهُۥ غَيۡبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ أَبۡصِرۡ بِهِۦ وَأَسۡمِعۡۚ مَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَلِيࣲّ وَلَا يُشۡرِكُ فِي حُكۡمِهِۦٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:26.en: Say: Allah is Best Aware how long they tarried. His is the Invisible of the heavens and the earth. How clear of sight is He and keen of hearing! They have no protecting friend beside Him, and He maketh none to share in His government

18:27.ar: وَٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن كِتَابِ رَبِّكَۖ لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَٰتِهِۦ وَلَن تَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلۡتَحَدࣰ ا
18:27.en: And recite that which hath been revealed unto thee of the Scripture of thy Lord. There is none who can change His words, and thou wilt find no refuge beside Him

18:28.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ نَفۡسَكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلۡعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَهُۥۖ وَلَا تَعۡدُ عَيۡنَاكَ عَنۡهُمۡ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَا تُطِعۡ مَنۡ أَغۡفَلۡنَا قَلۡبَهُۥ عَن ذِكۡرِنَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُهُۥ فُرُطࣰ ا
18:28.en: Restrain thyself along with those who cry unto their Lord at morn and evening, seeking His Countenance; and let not thine eyes overlook them, desiring the pomp of the life of the world; and obey not him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who followeth his own lust and whose case hath been abandoned

18:29.ar: وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ فَمَن شَآءَ فَلۡيُؤۡمِن وَمَن شَآءَ فَلۡيَكۡفُرۡۚ إِنَّآ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ نَارًا أَحَاطَ بِهِمۡ سُرَادِقُهَاۚ وَإِن يَسۡتَغِيثُواْ يُغَاثُواْ بِمَآءࣲ كَٱلۡمُهۡلِ يَشۡوِي ٱلۡوُجُوهَۚ بِئۡسَ ٱلشَّرَابُ وَسَآءَتۡ مُرۡتَفَقًا
18:29.en: Say: (It is) the truth from the Lord of you (all). Then whosoever will, let him believe, and whosoever will, let him disbelieve. Lo! We have prepared for disbelievers Fire. Its tent encloseth them. If they ask for showers, they will be showered with water like to molten lead which burneth the faces. Calamitous the drink and ill the resting-place

18:30.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ مَنۡ أَحۡسَنَ عَمَلًا
18:30.en: Lo! as for those who believe and do good works - Lo! We suffer not the reward of one whose work is goodly to be lost

18:31.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ عَدۡنࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهِمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ يُحَلَّوۡنَ فِيهَا مِنۡ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبࣲ وَيَلۡبَسُونَ ثِيَابًا خُضۡرࣰ ا مِّن سُندُسࣲ وَإِسۡتَبۡرَقࣲ مُّتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا عَلَى ٱلۡأَرَآئِكِۚ نِعۡمَ ٱلثَّوَابُ وَحَسُنَتۡ مُرۡتَفَقࣰ ا
18:31.en: As for such, theirs will be Gardens of Eden, wherein rivers flow beneath them; therein they will be given armlets of gold and will wear green robes of finest silk and gold embroidery, reclining upon throne therein. Blest the reward, and fair the resting-place

18:32.ar: ۞وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلࣰ ا رَّجُلَيۡنِ جَعَلۡنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيۡنِ مِنۡ أَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَحَفَفۡنَٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلࣲ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمَا زَرۡعࣰ ا
18:32.en: Coin for them a similitude: Two men, unto one of whom We had assigned two gardens of grapes, and We had surrounded both with date-palms and had put between them tillage

18:33.ar: كِلۡتَا ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ ءَاتَتۡ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمۡ تَظۡلِم مِّنۡهُ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَفَجَّرۡنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرࣰ ا
18:33.en: Each of the gardens gave its fruit and withheld naught thereof. And We caused a river to gush forth therein

18:34.ar: وَكَانَ لَهُۥ ثَمَرࣱ فَقَالَ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَنَا۠ أَكۡثَرُ مِنكَ مَالࣰ ا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرࣰ ا
18:34.en: And he had fruit. And he said unto his comrade, when he spake with him: I am more than thee in wealth, and stronger in respect of men

18:35.ar: وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمࣱ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدࣰ ا
18:35.en: And he went into his garden, while he (thus) wronged himself. He said: I think not that all this will ever perish

18:36.ar: وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةࣰ وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهَا مُنقَلَبࣰ ا
18:36.en: I think not that the Hour will ever come, and if indeed I am brought back unto my Lord I surely shall find better than this as a resort

18:37.ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ صَاحِبُهُۥ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَكَفَرۡتَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلࣰ ا
18:37.en: His comrade, when he (thus) spake with him, exclaimed: Disbelievest thou in Him Who created thee of dust, then of a drop (of seed), and then fashioned thee a man

18:38.ar: لَّٰكِنَّا۠ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:38.en: But He is Allah, my Lord, and I ascribe unto my Lord no partner

18:39.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ دَخَلۡتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلۡتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا۠ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالࣰ ا وَوَلَدࣰ ا
18:39.en: If only, when thou enteredst thy garden, thou hadst said: That which Allah willeth (will come to pass)! There is no strength save in Allah! Though thou seest me as less than thee in wealth and children

18:40.ar: فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَن يُؤۡتِيَنِ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡهَا حُسۡبَانࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصۡبِحَ صَعِيدࣰ ا زَلَقًا
18:40.en: Yet it may be that my Lord will give me better than thy garden, and will send on it a bolt from heaven, and some morning it will be a smooth hillside

18:41.ar: أَوۡ يُصۡبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوۡرࣰ ا فَلَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ لَهُۥ طَلَبࣰ ا
18:41.en: Or some morning the water thereof will be lost in the earth so that thou canst not make search for it

18:42.ar: وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِۦ فَأَصۡبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيۡهِ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُشۡرِكۡ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:42.en: And his fruit was beset (with destruction). Then began he to wring his hands for all that he had spent upon it, when (now) it was all ruined on its trellises, and to say: Would that I had ascribed no partner to my Lord

18:43.ar: وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ فِئَةࣱ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا
18:43.en: And he had no troop of men to help him as against Allah, nor could he save himself

18:44.ar: هُنَالِكَ ٱلۡوَلَٰيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ ثَوَابࣰ ا وَخَيۡرٌ عُقۡبࣰ ا
18:44.en: In this case is protection only from Allah, the True, He is Best for reward, and best for consequence

18:45.ar: وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخۡتَلَطَ بِهِۦ نَبَاتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَأَصۡبَحَ هَشِيمࣰ ا تَذۡرُوهُ ٱلرِّيَٰحُۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرًا
18:45.en: And coin for them the similitude of the life of the world as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingleth with it and then becometh dry twigs that the winds scatter. Allah is able to do all things

18:46.ar: ٱلۡمَالُ وَٱلۡبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَٱلۡبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيۡرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابࣰ ا وَخَيۡرٌ أَمَلࣰ ا
18:46.en: Wealth and children are an ornament of the life of the world. But the good deeds which endure are better in thy Lord's sight for reward, and better in respect of hope

18:47.ar: وَيَوۡمَ نُسَيِّرُ ٱلۡجِبَالَ وَتَرَى ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَارِزَةࣰ وَحَشَرۡنَٰهُمۡ فَلَمۡ نُغَادِرۡ مِنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:47.en: And (bethink you of) the Day when we remove the hills and ye see the earth emerging, and We gather them together so as to leave not one of them behind

18:48.ar: وَعُرِضُواْ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ صَفࣰّ ا لَّقَدۡ جِئۡتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةِۭۚ بَلۡ زَعَمۡتُمۡ أَلَّن نَّجۡعَلَ لَكُم مَّوۡعِدࣰ ا
18:48.en: And they are set before thy Lord in ranks (and it is said unto them): Now verily have ye come unto Us as We created you at the first. But ye thought that We had set no tryst for you

18:49.ar: وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةࣰ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَىٰهَاۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرࣰ اۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:49.en: And the Book is placed, and thou seest the guilty fearful of that which is therein, and they say: What kind of a Book is this that leaveth not a small thing nor a great thing but hath counted it! And they find all that they did confronting them, and thy Lord wrongeth no-one

18:50.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّهِۦٓۗ أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُۥ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِي وَهُمۡ لَكُمۡ عَدُوُّۢۚ بِئۡسَ لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَدَلࣰ ا
18:50.en: And (remember) when We said unto the angels: Fall prostrate before Adam, and they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He was of the jinn, so he rebelled against his Lord's command. Will ye choose him and his seed for your protecting friends instead of Me, when they are an enemy unto you? Calamitous is the exchange for evil-doers

18:51.ar: ۞مَّآ أَشۡهَدتُّهُمۡ خَلۡقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا خَلۡقَ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَمَا كُنتُ مُتَّخِذَ ٱلۡمُضِلِّينَ عَضُدࣰ ا
18:51.en: I made them not to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation; nor choose I misleaders for (My) helpers

18:52.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَقُولُ نَادُواْ شُرَكَآءِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُمۡ فَدَعَوۡهُمۡ فَلَمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَهُمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُم مَّوۡبِقࣰ ا
18:52.en: And (be mindful of) the Day when He will say: Call those partners of Mine whom ye pretended. Then they will cry unto them, but they will not hear their prayer, and We shall set a gulf of doom between them

18:53.ar: وَرَءَا ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ ٱلنَّارَ فَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مُّوَاقِعُوهَا وَلَمۡ يَجِدُواْ عَنۡهَا مَصۡرِفࣰ ا
18:53.en: And the guilty behold the Fire and know that they are about to fall therein, and they find no way of escape thence

18:54.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا فِي هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ لِلنَّاسِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلࣲۚ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ أَكۡثَرَ شَيۡءࣲ جَدَلࣰ ا
18:54.en: And verily We have displayed for mankind in this Qur'an all manner of similitudes, but man is more than anything contentious

18:55.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤۡمِنُوٓاْ إِذۡ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَيَسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن تَأۡتِيَهُمۡ سُنَّةُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ قُبُلࣰ ا
18:55.en: And naught hindereth mankind from believing when the guidance cometh unto them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord unless (it be that they wish) that the judgment of the men of old should come upon them or (that) they should be confronted with the Doom

17:62.ar: قَالَ أَرَءَيۡتَكَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كَرَّمۡتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنۡ أَخَّرۡتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَأَحۡتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:62.en: He said: Seest Thou this (creature) whom Thou hast honoured above me, if Thou give me grace until the Day of Resurrection I verily will seize his seed, save but a few

17:63.ar: قَالَ ٱذۡهَبۡ فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمۡ جَزَآءࣰ مَّوۡفُورࣰ ا
17:63.en: He said: Go, and whosoever of them followeth thee - lo! hell will be your payment, ample payment

17:64.ar: وَٱسۡتَفۡزِزۡ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتَ مِنۡهُم بِصَوۡتِكَ وَأَجۡلِبۡ عَلَيۡهِم بِخَيۡلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ وَشَارِكۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَوۡلَٰدِ وَعِدۡهُمۡۚ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا
17:64.en: And excite any of them whom thou canst with thy voice, and urge thy horse and foot against them, and be a partner in their wealth and children, and promise them. Satan promiseth them only to deceive

17:65.ar: إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيۡسَ لَكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سُلۡطَٰنࣱۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلࣰ ا
17:65.en: Lo! My (faithful) bondmen - over them thou hast no power, and thy Lord sufficeth as (their) guardian

17:66.ar: رَّبُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي يُزۡجِي لَكُمُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ لِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِكُمۡ رَحِيمࣰ ا
17:66.en: (O mankind), your Lord is He Who driveth for you the ship upon the sea that ye may seek of His bounty. Lo! He was ever Merciful toward you

17:67.ar: وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدۡعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُۖ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ أَعۡرَضۡتُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ كَفُورًا
17:67.en: And when harm toucheth you upon the sea, all unto whom ye cry (for succour) fail save Him (alone), but when He bringeth you safe to land, ye turn away, for man was ever thankless

17:68.ar: أَفَأَمِنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمۡ جَانِبَ ٱلۡبَرِّ أَوۡ يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبࣰ ا ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُواْ لَكُمۡ وَكِيلًا
17:68.en: Feel ye then secure that He will not cause a slope of the land to engulf you, or send a sand-storm upon you, and then ye will find that ye have no protector

17:69.ar: أَمۡ أَمِنتُمۡ أَن يُعِيدَكُمۡ فِيهِ تَارَةً أُخۡرَىٰ فَيُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ قَاصِفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلرِّيحِ فَيُغۡرِقَكُم بِمَا كَفَرۡتُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُواْ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا بِهِۦ تَبِيعࣰ ا
17:69.en: Or feel ye secure that He will not return you to that (plight) a second time, and send against you a hurricane of wind and drown you for your thanklessness, and then ye will not find therein that ye have any avenger against Us

17:70.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ كَرَّمۡنَا بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَرَزَقۡنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرࣲ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقۡنَا تَفۡضِيلࣰ ا
17:70.en: Verily we have honoured the Children of Adam. We carry them on the land and the sea, and have made provision of good things for them, and have preferred them above many of those whom We created with a marked preferment

17:73.ar: وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَفۡتِنُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ لِتَفۡتَرِيَ عَلَيۡنَا غَيۡرَهُۥۖ وَإِذࣰ ا لَّٱتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلࣰ ا
17:73.en: And they indeed strove hard to beguile thee (Muhammad) away from that wherewith We have inspired thee, that thou shouldst invent other than it against Us; and then would they have accepted thee as a friend

17:74.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن ثَبَّتۡنَٰكَ لَقَدۡ كِدتَّ تَرۡكَنُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا قَلِيلًا
17:74.en: And if We had not made thee wholly firm thou mightest almost have inclined unto them a little

17:75.ar: إِذࣰ ا لَّأَذَقۡنَٰكَ ضِعۡفَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ وَضِعۡفَ ٱلۡمَمَاتِ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ عَلَيۡنَا نَصِيرࣰ ا
17:75.en: Then had we made thee taste a double (punishment) of living and a double (punishment) of dying, then hadst thou found no helper against Us

17:76.ar: وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسۡتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُخۡرِجُوكَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَإِذࣰ ا لَّا يَلۡبَثُونَ خِلَٰفَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:76.en: And they indeed wished to scare thee from the land that they might drive thee forth from thence, and then they would have stayed (there) but a little after thee

17:77.ar: سُنَّةَ مَن قَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا قَبۡلَكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَاۖ وَلَا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحۡوِيلًا
17:77.en: (Such was Our) method in the case of those whom We sent before thee (to mankind), and thou wilt not find for Our method aught of power to change

17:78.ar: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَقُرۡءَانَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِۖ إِنَّ قُرۡءَانَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ كَانَ مَشۡهُودࣰ ا
17:78.en: Establish worship at the going down of the sun until the dark of night, and (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn. Lo! (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed

17:79.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَتَهَجَّدۡ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةࣰ لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبۡعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامࣰ ا مَّحۡمُودࣰ ا
17:79.en: And some part of the night awake for it, a largess for thee. It may be that thy Lord will raise thee to a praised estate

17:80.ar: وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدۡخِلۡنِي مُدۡخَلَ صِدۡقࣲ وَأَخۡرِجۡنِي مُخۡرَجَ صِدۡقࣲ وَٱجۡعَل لِّي مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا نَّصِيرࣰ ا
17:80.en: And say: My Lord! Cause me to come in with a firm incoming and to go out with a firm outgoing. And give me from Thy presence a sustaining Power

17:81.ar: وَقُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقࣰ ا
17:81.en: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish

17:82.ar: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مَا هُوَ شِفَآءࣱ وَرَحۡمَةࣱ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارࣰ ا
17:82.en: And We reveal of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for believers though it increase the evil-doers in naught save ruin

17:83.ar: وَإِذَآ أَنۡعَمۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ أَعۡرَضَ وَنَـَٔا بِجَانِبِهِۦ وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ كَانَ يَـُٔوسࣰ ا
17:83.en: And when We make life pleasant unto man, he turneth away and is averse; and when ill toucheth him he is in despair

17:84.ar: قُلۡ كُلࣱّ يَعۡمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِۦ فَرَبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنۡ هُوَ أَهۡدَىٰ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:84.en: Say: Each one doth according to his rule of conduct, and thy Lord is Best Aware of him whose way is right

17:85.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّي وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:85.en: They are asking thee concerning the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is by command of my Lord, and of knowledge ye have been vouchsafed but little

17:86.ar: وَلَئِن شِئۡنَا لَنَذۡهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِۦ عَلَيۡنَا وَكِيلًا
17:86.en: And if We willed We could withdraw that which We have revealed unto thee, then wouldst thou find no guardian for thee against Us in respect thereof

17:87.ar: إِلَّا رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَۚ إِنَّ فَضۡلَهُۥ كَانَ عَلَيۡكَ كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:87.en: (It is naught) save mercy from thy Lord. Lo! His kindness unto thee was ever great

17:88.ar: قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجۡتَمَعَتِ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتُواْ بِمِثۡلِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ لَا يَأۡتُونَ بِمِثۡلِهِۦ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضࣲ ظَهِيرࣰ ا
17:88.en: Say: Verily, though mankind and the jinn should assemble to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like thereof though they were helpers one of another

17:89.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلࣲ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورࣰ ا
17:89.en: And verily We have displayed for mankind in this Qur'an all kind of similitudes, but most of mankind refuse aught save disbelief

17:90.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفۡجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
17:90.en: And they say: We will not put faith in thee till thou cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us

17:91.ar: أَوۡ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةࣱ مِّن نَّخِيلࣲ وَعِنَبࣲ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفۡجِيرًا
17:91.en: Or thou have a garden of date-palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth therein abundantly

17:92.ar: أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفًا أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
17:92.en: Or thou cause the heaven to fall upon us piecemeal, as thou hast pretended, or bring Allah and the angels as a warrant

17:93.ar: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتࣱ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبࣰ ا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا رَّسُولࣰ ا
17:93.en: Or thou have a house of gold; or thou ascend up into heaven, and even then we will put no faith in thine ascension till thou bring down for us a book that we can read. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord be Glorified! Am I aught save a mortal messenger

17:105.ar: وَبِٱلۡحَقِّ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ وَبِٱلۡحَقِّ نَزَلَۗ وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا
17:105.en: With truth have We sent it down, and with truth hath it descended. And We have sent thee as naught else save a bearer of good tidings and a warner

17:106.ar: وَقُرۡءَانࣰ ا فَرَقۡنَٰهُ لِتَقۡرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكۡثࣲ وَنَزَّلۡنَٰهُ تَنزِيلࣰ ا
17:106.en: And (it is) a Qur'an that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by (successive) revelation

17:107.ar: قُلۡ ءَامِنُواْ بِهِۦٓ أَوۡ لَا تُؤۡمِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦٓ إِذَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ يَخِرُّونَۤ لِلۡأَذۡقَانِۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ
17:107.en: Say: Believe therein or believe not, lo! those who were given knowledge before it, when it is read unto them, fall down prostrate on their faces, adoring

17:108.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِن كَانَ وَعۡدُ رَبِّنَا لَمَفۡعُولࣰ ا
17:108.en: Saying: Glory to our Lord! Verily the promise of our Lord must be fulfilled

17:109.ar: وَيَخِرُّونَ لِلۡأَذۡقَانِ يَبۡكُونَ وَيَزِيدُهُمۡ خُشُوعࣰ ا۩
17:109.en: They fall down on their faces, weeping, and it increaseth humility in them

17:110.ar: قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَۖ أَيࣰّ ا مَّا تَدۡعُواْ فَلَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَلَا تَجۡهَرۡ بِصَلَاتِكَ وَلَا تُخَافِتۡ بِهَا وَٱبۡتَغِ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:110.en: Say (unto mankind): Cry unto Allah, or cry unto the Beneficent, unto whichsoever ye cry (it is the same). His are the most beautiful names. And thou (Muhammad), be not loud-voiced in thy worship nor yet silent therein, but follow a way between

17:111.ar: وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكࣱ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِيࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّۖ وَكَبِّرۡهُ تَكۡبِيرَۢا
17:111.en: And say: Praise be to Allah, Who hath not taken unto Himself a son, and Who hath no partner in the Sovereignty, nor hath He any protecting friend through dependence. And magnify Him with all magnificence

Vk2cIJ23_5Y.speaker: adnan
Vk2cIJ23_5Y.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day Ramadan series; same format and voice as other episodes
Vk2cIJ23_5Y.title: A Juz A Day: Juz 15, The Values of the Glorious Quran
Vk2cIJ23_5Y.one_line: Surat al-Isra as a surah about the Quran and its values, then the opening of al-Kahf and its trials of life.
Vk2cIJ23_5Y.summary: He walks through Juz 15, presenting al-Isra as a surah about the greatness of the Quran. The night journey marks the passing of the torch of revelation from the Israelites to the Prophet's nation, and the Israelites' two destructions warn that abandoning revelation brings ruin; he applies this directly to today's ummah, whose Quran lives in classrooms rather than running societies. He stresses individual accountability: no one carries another's burden, so no one can blame society for their own failings. The core of the session is the passage of commandments from 17:22 onward, which he numbers one by one: worship Allah alone, honour parents, give to relatives, avoid waste, balance spending, do not kill children or approach zina, respect life and the orphan's wealth, keep pledges, give fair measure, act only on knowledge and avoid arrogance. He then covers Iblis's playbook, the Quran protecting the Prophet from compromising principle, the sweetness of Fajr and night prayer, and the Quran's inimitability. Moving to al-Kahf, he frames its stories as five trials (faith under persecution, wealth, the Day of Judgment, knowledge, power) and explains the youth of the cave and the owner of the two gardens, concluding that wealth is no sign of Allah's pleasure and that the Quran is the means to survive life's trials.

outline.heading: Juz 15: the halfway mark, al-Isra and al-Kahf
outline.gist: He sets the range of the juz from the start of al-Isra to 18:74.

outline.heading: The night journey and the names of the two mosques
outline.gist: Why the Sacred Mosque and the Furthest Mosque are named so, and the events of Isra and Mi'raj including the command of salah.

outline.heading: A surah about the Quran: the torch passes to the Prophet's nation
outline.gist: The word Quran appears eleven times; the Prophet leading the prophets in prayer symbolizes leadership of revelation moving on, as it moved before from Nuh's people to Musa's.

outline.heading: The two destructions of the Israelites
outline.gist: When they abandoned the scripture they were devastated twice; repentance brings mercy and return to sin brings return of punishment.

outline.heading: The ummah's weakness from abandoning the Quran
outline.gist: Today the Quran's teachings are confined to classrooms rather than running societies, and the ummah's state follows the same law.

outline.heading: The Quran guides to what is most upright: warning and good news together
outline.gist: Only warning falls on deaf ears and only good news is a sugar high; the combination brings real change.

outline.heading: Destiny bound to the neck and the open record
outline.gist: Every person receives their record and is sufficient to judge themselves.

outline.heading: No soul bears another's burden; no punishment before a messenger
outline.gist: Individual accountability, and Allah weighs how fully the message reached each person.

outline.heading: You cannot blame society for your choices
outline.gist: Saying society made me materialistic is no excuse; this is one of the most profound principles of the Quran.

outline.heading: Destroying a society whose elite rebel
outline.gist: Punishment falls when a society's elite act corruptly after being commanded to obey.

outline.heading: Those who want only this world versus those who strive for the next
outline.gist: What Allah gives in this life is no indicator of His pleasure; striving for the hereafter is what is appreciated.

outline.heading: Commandment one: worship Allah alone
outline.gist: The passage of commandments begins: set up no other god besides Allah.

outline.heading: Commandment two: honour your parents
outline.gist: Worship none but Him, then honour parents: not even a sigh of displeasure, humility out of mercy, and dua for them.

outline.heading: Commandment three: give relatives, the poor and travellers their due
outline.gist: Spending on those close to us and those in need, and the warning that the wasteful are brothers of the devils.

outline.heading: Commandment four: do not waste, and give a kind word when you cannot give
outline.gist: Waste belittles Allah's favour; if you have nothing, decline gently and kindly.

outline.heading: Commandment five: neither tight-fisted nor open-handed
outline.gist: The image of a hand chained to the neck versus a fully open hand; both leave you blameworthy and stuck.

outline.heading: Provision is Allah's choice, not a measure of worth
outline.gist: Some vile people are wealthy and some upright people struggle; wealth signals neither Allah's pleasure nor a person's value.

outline.heading: Commandment six: do not kill children for fear of poverty
outline.gist: Allah provides for them and for you.

outline.heading: Commandment seven: do not even approach zina
outline.gist: Cutting the root cause, since many abortions follow unplanned pregnancies outside marriage.

outline.heading: Commandment eight: sanctity of life and justice through the courts
outline.gist: Legal right means a court process, never vigilante justice, and heirs must not exceed limits.

outline.heading: Commandment nine: the orphan's wealth
outline.gist: Approach an orphan's property only to grow it, followed by honouring pledges and giving full measure.

outline.heading: Commandment eleven: do not follow what you have no knowledge of
outline.gist: The practice of Islam and one's worldview must be built on knowledge; hearing, sight and intellect will be questioned.

outline.heading: Commandment twelve: do not walk arrogantly
outline.gist: You cannot crack the earth or reach the mountains; pride comes before the fall.

outline.heading: A walking Quran: what these values represent
outline.gist: This passage shows part of what it means to be a person of the Quran.

outline.heading: Everything glorifies Allah
outline.gist: Our glorification is for our own benefit, as all creation praises Him in ways we cannot comprehend.

outline.heading: Those veiled from benefiting from the Quran
outline.gist: Quraysh secretly listened at night, mesmerized, yet it did not change them, so they called the Prophet bewitched.

outline.heading: Resurrection: the one who created you first will recreate you
outline.gist: Asking when it will happen is misdirection once the logic is undeniable; on that day people will rise praising Him.

outline.heading: Iblis's playbook: voice, cavalry, wealth and children
outline.gist: His voice as distraction and wasted time, human devils as his troops, and inflating the value of wealth and family; he has no authority over faithful servants.

outline.heading: Ships at sea and turning to Allah only in adversity
outline.gist: People take the systems Allah made for granted and remember Him only when in danger.

outline.heading: Allah has dignified the children of Adam
outline.gist: Allah honours humanity while Shaytan seeks to debase it.

outline.heading: The Quran kept the Prophet from compromising principle
outline.gist: Policy compromises like Hudaybiyyah are fine, but no compromise on worship or the source of morality; the Quran protects us from social pressure too.

outline.heading: Driven out of Makkah, and Allah's unchanging way
outline.gist: Within a few years of leaving he returned to bring Makkah under Islam.

outline.heading: The sweetness of the Quran in Fajr and night prayer
outline.gist: Fajr recitation is witnessed and night prayer gives a connection like no other time.

outline.heading: Dua for an honourable entry and exit; falsehood vanishes
outline.gist: A dua for any tricky circumstance, and the nature of falsehood to perish.

outline.heading: Quran as healing; ingratitude and lack of resilience
outline.gist: People turn away when blessed and lose all hope at the slightest adversity.

outline.heading: The spirit, and the Quran's inimitability
outline.gist: Little knowledge has been given about the soul; humans and jinn together cannot produce the like of the Quran.

outline.heading: Ridiculous demands and the reply: I am only a human messenger
outline.gist: When claims are too absurd to refute, state a simple truth.

outline.heading: Revealed in stages to be recited deliberately
outline.gist: Gradual revelation lets it enter hearts and be processed.

outline.heading: Those given knowledge fall weeping in prostration
outline.gist: Recognizing the truth of revelation and the feeling of sujud in humility is one of life's greatest feelings.

outline.heading: Calling on Allah by His beautiful names; moderate recitation
outline.gist: Make dua through His names, and recite neither too loudly nor too silently.

qIW9_QwdA1s.title: The Values of Islam: Rahmah (Compassion) and Rifq (Tenderness)
qIW9_QwdA1s.one_line: Rahmah is a universal human right and the bare minimum of how a Muslim treats anyone, even enemies and tyrants; rifq is how it is applied.
qIW9_QwdA1s.summary: The sheikh calls rahmah the value most associated with the Prophet, who was not only described with mercy but described as mercy itself. Hadith students traditionally begin with the narration that the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Rooted in the word for womb, rahmah means providing a safe space for growth and acknowledging human fragility, and rifq, tenderness, is its practice: you cannot hammer glass and wonder why it shatters. Borrowing from medical testing, he calls rahmah a highly sensitive test of Islam: its absence proves Islam is absent, and if learning makes you harsher, your teacher is teaching something else. Rahmah is a human right with no exceptions; punishments exist out of mercy to the collective, but even the condemned keep their dignity. He laments that torture marks many Muslim countries that perfect ritual while losing ethics, and contrasts the testimony of released Palestinian and Israeli prisoners. Prophetic examples include the sheep that must not see the blade and the bird whose eggs were returned. Rahmah allows firmness, as with parents who set consequences, but without rifq firmness becomes domination and trauma. An ethic that is not universal is only a preference: you need not love your enemy, but you can always show him mercy.

outline.heading: A value that is also an ethic
outline.gist: Rahmah judges many behaviours and belongs at the top, though he places it mid-series.

outline.heading: The Prophet as mercy itself

outline.heading: Rooted in the womb
outline.gist: Rahmah means giving people a safe space to exist and grow.

outline.heading: Acknowledging fragility
outline.gist: Compassion understands people can break, which is where rifq comes in; Allah is gentle and loves gentleness.

outline.heading: Tenderness beautifies everything
outline.gist: Rifq improves whatever it enters; you cannot hammer glass and wonder why it shatters.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim
outline.gist: The Prophet saw people's weakness; Allah is best known by two names from this root.

outline.heading: A highly sensitive test of being Muslim
outline.gist: Like a medical test, if rahmah is absent, Islam is absent, though its presence does not prove Islam.

outline.heading: If learning makes you harsher
outline.gist: Growing in knowledge while shrinking in empathy means you are being taught something other than Islam.

outline.heading: Rahmah is a human right
outline.gist: Everyone deserves it, even enemies and dictators; it is the floor below which a Muslim never goes.

outline.heading: Punishment as mercy to the collective
outline.gist: Strict legal punishments protect society, but are carried out with mercy and dignity.

outline.heading: Cells where you are treated like dirt
outline.gist: Torture has become the mark of Middle Eastern states, because ethics were lost.

outline.heading: Ritual without ethics
outline.gist: Countries that perfect prayer lines but abandon ethics have missed the point.

outline.heading: Fiqh differs, ethics do not
outline.gist: People fight over juristic details that allow difference while the unchanging ethics are non-negotiable.

outline.heading: Do not kill the sheep twice
outline.gist: The Prophet rebuked a man sharpening his knife in front of the animal he was dragging.

outline.heading: The mother bird's eggs
outline.gist: During a campaign he had a young man return the eggs he took from a nest.

outline.heading: Mercy even in war
outline.gist: He never hated his enemies, accepted their repentance and forbade harming trees, children, women, homes and worshippers.

outline.heading: Mercy can mean strictness
outline.gist: A merciful parent denies a child endless TV and ice cream; without rahmah comes domination, without rifq trauma.

outline.heading: Consequences at home
outline.gist: Truth and authority applied with tenderness form children morally, and a consequence at home is cheaper than one outside.

outline.heading: Rahmah is not weakness
outline.gist: It stands its ground and may apply strict punishment when the community needs it.

outline.heading: Dignity in custody
outline.gist: Incarceration can be dignified or brutal; Muslims held human dignity as a right a thousand years before the UN.

outline.heading: How we lost it
outline.gist: Not only governments but peoples now speak of enemies without mercy.

outline.heading: Two sets of released prisoners
outline.gist: Compare the trauma of released Palestinian prisoners with the accounts of returned Israeli captives.

outline.heading: Everyone or no one
outline.gist: You may not decide who is an exception to a right.

outline.heading: Even the tyrant
outline.gist: Tried and executed, but with mercy, because it defines us; Jahannam is Allah's justice, not our job.

outline.heading: A non-universal ethic is a preference
outline.gist: If mercy does not apply to everyone, it is only a convenience.

outline.heading: Not love thy enemy, but mercy
outline.gist: You cannot love someone trying to destroy you, but you can show him mercy, even in a bitter divorce.

outline.heading: When every other ethic fails
outline.gist: Love, respect and more can fail, but compassion can always be brought; rifq is the spice of life.

A0rM9YPtLQk.title: Third Week of Ramadan: Showing Commitment to Change
A0rM9YPtLQk.one_line: Mid-Ramadan: solidify the changes of the first two weeks into lifelong habits, expect tests, and learn from the Sahabah whose first Ramadan was Badr.
A0rM9YPtLQk.summary: He opens with 9:105, act and Allah, His Messenger and the believers will see your deeds, then turns to the news: eight countries bombed in days, the lands that produced Islam's early scholars being destroyed. He avoids politics, since three hundred people hold three thousand opinions, but insists on dua for the people of Sham, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen, the Gulf, Iran and Sudan, argues that any Muslim unity would have stopped the tyrants, and tells Muslims in the West to use the seat at the table they have. Ramadan is a time-out for looking inward, and the Quran starts with the individual: you cannot predict geopolitics, but you control what you intend, do and stand for. Two weeks of fasting and night prayer already show an impressive change; now it must be solidified into lifelong, not Ramadanic, habits, guarded from the distraction of wealth and family, built on small consistent deeds. Commitment will be tested, as 29:10 warns, and Ramadan gives four weeks to build that capacity. The Sahabah's first Ramadan brought Badr: called to reclaim their stolen goods they argued they no longer needed the money, but it was about standing for truth, since there is no dignity in surrendering what was taken from you. Outnumbered, the first army in Arabia bound by moral glue rather than blood won the day that separated truth from falsehood. He asks everyone to keep their new habits for months and report back.

outline.heading: Opening
Act, and Allah will see your deeds
outline.gist: 9:105: live your life and do what you will, for Allah, His Messenger and the believers witness it, and you will be returned to your Lord to be held to account.

outline.heading: The birthplace of the deen under bombardment
outline.gist: Every quiet period ends in more death in the region where Islam was born. Islam reached every continent because of the early scholars of Sham, Iraq, Iran and Arabia who taught, documented and protected it, and every part of that land is being destroyed; eight countries bombed in a few days.

outline.heading: Not politics, but the people
outline.gist: He stays out of the region's politics, where three hundred people hold three thousand opinions driven by emotion, and focuses on what all agree on: the wellbeing of people who lived their whole lives under regimes that cared nothing for their rights.

outline.heading: Make dua for them
outline.gist: Every colour in the room came from that land, and if life there were good no one would have left. Make dua for the people of Sham, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen, the Gulf, Iran and Sudan, who were barely making ends meet before the bombs.

outline.heading: Unity stops tyrants, and a voice at the table
outline.gist: Any Muslim unity on any front would have prevented this; powers that cannot let a decade pass without war itch to bomb brown people. Muslims in the West must also advocate, because they can sit at the table where others cannot.

outline.heading: Ramadan is a time-out
outline.gist: No better time for this message than Ramadan, when you step back, look inward and ask what you are doing with your life and whether you live it meaningfully for Allah.

outline.heading: The Quran starts with the individual
outline.gist: You cannot predict international politics, but you can control what you feel, intend, think and do: your participation, your contribution and where you stand.

outline.heading: Two weeks of impressive change
outline.gist: Two full weeks of fasting every day and praying every night speak to your character; anyone observing you would see a person less distracted, more focused and devoted than before Ramadan.

outline.heading: Do not let wealth and family distract you
outline.gist: Now solidify the commitment. 63:9: wealth and children, the two closest blessings you rightly thank Allah for, must never distract you from remembering Him and why He created you.

outline.heading: Small consistent deeds
outline.gist: When you change, know what you are moving towards and what you leave behind. The most beloved deeds to Allah are the consistent ones, even small, simple ones no one will thank you for; that is how change begins.

outline.heading: Lifelong habits, not Ramadanic habits
outline.gist: No one can fast and pray every night after Ramadan, but pick the positive changes you want to hold on to as a way of showing Allah your commitment, and plan them as habits that define who you are.

outline.heading: Commitment will be tested
outline.gist: 29:10: some claim commitment until they are harmed for Allah's sake, then treat people's trial as worse than Allah's punishment and step back. Real change always meets obstacles that test how much pushback you will take; Allah will not let us off the hook that easily, and Ramadan comes four weeks in a row to build that capacity.

outline.heading: The Sahabah's first Ramadan
outline.gist: On a day like this, 1445 lunar years ago, Ramadan was defined to them for the first time: the doors of heaven opened, the doors of Jahannam closed, the devils removed, a night better than a lifetime. A little perseverance for an amazing deal.

outline.heading: The 17th: a call to reclaim the stolen caravan
outline.gist: Ramadan with the Prophet, who often prayed at home to keep things easy for them. On the morning of the 17th he called them out to intercept the caravan Abu Sufyan was leading with the wealth Quraysh had confiscated from them for their belief.

outline.heading: Reluctance before Badr (8:5-7)
outline.gist: After two years in Madinah they had wealth and argued they would give up their stolen property for Allah's sake, when deep down they did not want to provoke Quraysh. 8:5-7: your Lord brought you out in truth while a party of believers were averse, arguing as if driven to death, wishing for the unarmed caravan.

outline.heading: Refuse oppression however it is packaged
outline.gist: It was about righteousness, not money. A Muslim stands up against transgression whatever mask it wears. Take back what is rightfully yours, then gift it if you wish; surrendering what was taken by force is neither courage, generosity nor dignity.

outline.heading: Makkah held on, Madinah had to embody
outline.gist: For thirteen years in Makkah they were told not to bear arms and only had to persevere and hold on to the deen. In Madinah, with a country, holding on was no longer enough: they had to carry Islam's values everywhere.

outline.heading: Righteousness has to be demonstrated
outline.gist: Islam stands for the truth at all times, beyond dispute; the Quran exposed their reluctance because the truth had to be shown. It was a frightening day: 313 or 314 men with the Prophet, and scholars differ on the number.

outline.heading: The caravan escapes, Quraysh marches
outline.gist: Abu Sufyan anticipated them and took another route. At Badr the caravan was gone and Quraysh marched with a thousand men and more cavalry than the entire Muslim army, which had two horsemen and little training or arms.

outline.heading: An army of moral glue
outline.gist: Facing the undefeated champion of the region, for the first time in Arabia an army stood together not on tribe, blood, vengeance or raiding but on a shared cause: a Qurashi beside an Ansari beside a man from the Roman Empire.

outline.heading: The day truth and falsehood separated
outline.gist: They fought bravely; the best of the companions are the people of Badr and the best of the angels those who helped them. After that day it was clear who stood on which side, beginning the chain of events that fills this masjid.

outline.heading: Interlude
Second khutbah: prove your commitment
outline.gist: Ramadan is the chance to show Allah the commitment to change, as the Sahabah did in their first Ramadan when sent, unprepared, outnumbered and uncertain, against the strongest power in the region; they proved it, and every good thing in the deen followed.

outline.heading: Keep it for a few months, then report back
outline.gist: Turn small changes into daily habits: a little fasting, more dhikr, night prayer, daily learning about Allah. Hold on to them for a few months after Ramadan, then come and tell him how your life, mind and commitment have changed.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Mid-Ramadan as a time-out to look inward and the moment to solidify two weeks of change into lasting habits; the month comes four weeks in a row to build capacity, and the Sahabah's first Ramadan was Badr.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Every Ramadan offers the chance to prove the commitment to change and to turn small changes into daily habits kept for months afterwards.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Change begins with the individual: control your intentions, actions and stance, keep the positive habits of Ramadan as lifelong and identity-defining habits, and value small consistent deeds over flashy ones.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Badr retold as the Sahabah's test of commitment in their first Ramadan: the reluctant response to the call, the escaped caravan, 313 men against a thousand, and the first army in Arabia bound by conviction rather than blood.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: Commitment means holding your ground when challenges stack up; those who retreat at the first harm never truly committed, and Allah will not let real change go untested.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: A Muslim stands against transgression however it is masked; surrendering what was taken by force is neither generosity nor dignity, so reclaim it and then give it away if you choose.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Eight countries bombed in days; the region that nurtured Islam is being systematically destroyed by tyranny, civil war and foreign bombing, and its people deserve our dua.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Ramadan is the time to step back and ask what you are doing with your life and whether you live meaningfully for Allah; an observer would see a clear difference between you before and during Ramadan.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Turning the ship around guarantees obstacles placed to test how much difficulty you will bear; it is part of life, not a sign to quit.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Any form of Muslim unity on any front would have prevented this; unity stops tyrants, and it is what Muslims must strive toward.

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward
themes.note: Muslims in the West have a voice and a seat at the table that others lack, and must use it to reflect the values and concerns of the voiceless.

themes.label: Islamic history and civilization
themes.note: Islam reached every continent because of the early scholars of Sham, Iraq, Iran and Arabia who taught, documented, protected and spread it.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Wealth and family are the two closest blessings and the two most likely distractions from remembering Allah and your purpose.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: The people of Badr are the best of the companions; their army united Qurashi, Ansari, Abyssinian and Roman by moral glue, and that day separated truth from falsehood.

quran.point: Do as you will, for Allah, His Messenger and the believers will see your deeds and you will be returned to your Lord for account. The opening verse on visible commitment.
Do not let your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah; the two closest blessings must not become distractions.
Some say they believe but when harmed for Allah's sake treat people's trial like Allah's punishment; the picture of commitment that collapses at the first difficulty.

Your Lord brought you out of your home in truth while a party of believers were averse, arguing about the truth as if driven to death, after Allah promised one of the two groups. The Sahabah's reluctance before Badr.

hadith.gist: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the consistent ones, even if small and unremarkable.
In Ramadan the doors of heaven are opened, the doors of Jahannam closed and the devils removed, and a night better than a lifetime is granted.
The best of the companions are those who were at Badr, and the Prophet said the best of the angels were those who helped at Badr.

maxims: Ramadan is a time-out
Not Ramadanic habits but lifelong habits
Allah won't let us off the hook that easy
There is no courage in giving up what was taken from you
Take back what is yours, then gift it if you want
Three hundred people in a room, three thousand opinions on politics

stories.who: The Sahabah's first Ramadan and Badr
stories.point: Excited by Ramadan's promises, they were called on the 17th to reclaim their confiscated wealth, argued they no longer needed it, and were taught that the matter was righteousness, not money; their commitment was tested by the strongest power in the region.

stories.who: Makkah versus Madinah
stories.point: For thirteen years their task was to hold on under oppression; in Madinah, with a country, they had to carry and embody Islam's values everywhere, not just endure.

stories.who: The first army of moral glue
stories.point: Outnumbered and unprepared, 313 men from every background stood together by conviction rather than tribe or vengeance, and that day made truth and falsehood unmistakable.

contemporary: Eight countries bombed in the preceding days; Sham, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen, the Gulf, Iran and Sudan named for dua
The region that produced Islam's early scholars being destroyed by tyranny, civil war and bombing
Powers that cannot let a decade pass without a major war, described as itching to bomb brown people
Muslims in the West having a seat at the table that others lack
15 Ramadan 1447
takeaways: Make dua for the people of the bombed region, strive for Muslim unity, and use your voice in the West to advocate for those who have none.
Use Ramadan as a time-out to look inward and focus on what you control: your intentions, participation and stance.
Pick the positive changes of the first two weeks and plan to keep them as lifelong habits built on small consistent deeds.
Expect obstacles when you commit to change and hold your ground instead of retreating at the first test.
Stand for truth and against oppression always; reclaim what is rightfully yours rather than calling surrender generosity, and report back months after Ramadan on how your life changed.

12:1.en: Alif. Lam. Ra. These are verse of the Scripture that maketh plain

12:2.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ قُرۡءَٰنًا عَرَبِيࣰّ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
12:2.en: Lo! We have revealed it, a Lecture in Arabic, that ye may understand

12:3.ar: نَحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلۡغَٰفِلِينَ
12:3.en: We narrate unto thee (Muhammad) the best of narratives in that We have inspired in thee this Qur'an, though aforetime thou wast of the heedless

12:4.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيۡتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوۡكَبࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ رَأَيۡتُهُمۡ لِي سَٰجِدِينَ
12:4.en: When Joseph said unto his father: O my father! Lo! I saw in a dream eleven planets and the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating themselves unto me

12:5.ar: قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ لَا تَقۡصُصۡ رُءۡيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُواْ لَكَ كَيۡدًاۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
12:5.en: He said: O my dear son! Tell not thy brethren of thy vision, lest they plot a plot against thee. Lo! Satan is for man an open foe

12:6.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجۡتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعۡمَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعۡقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيۡكَ مِن قَبۡلُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
12:6.en: Thus thy Lord will prefer thee and will teach thee the interpretation of events, and will perfect His grace upon thee and upon the family of Jacob as He perfected it upon thy forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. Lo! thy Lord is Knower, Wise

12:7.ar: ۞لَّقَدۡ كَانَ فِي يُوسُفَ وَإِخۡوَتِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتࣱ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
12:7.en: Verily in Joseph and his brethren are signs (of Allah's Sovereignty) for the inquiring

12:8.ar: إِذۡ قَالُواْ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحۡنُ عُصۡبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
12:8.en: When they said: Verily Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, many though we be. Lo! our father is in plain aberration

12:9.ar: ٱقۡتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطۡرَحُوهُ أَرۡضࣰ ا يَخۡلُ لَكُمۡ وَجۡهُ أَبِيكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ قَوۡمࣰ ا صَٰلِحِينَ
12:9.en: (One said): Kill Joseph or cast him to some (other) land, so that your father's favour may be all for you, and (that) ye may afterward be righteous folk
