36:45.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُواْ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيكُمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
36:45.en: When it is said unto them: Beware of that which is before you and that which is behind you, that haply ye may find mercy (they are heedless)

36:46.ar: وَمَا تَأۡتِيهِم مِّنۡ ءَايَةࣲ مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ إِلَّا كَانُواْ عَنۡهَا مُعۡرِضِينَ
36:46.en: Never came a token of the tokens of their Lord to them, but they did turn away from it

36:47.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ أَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنُطۡعِمُ مَن لَّوۡ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ أَطۡعَمَهُۥٓ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
36:47.en: And when it is said unto them: Spend of that wherewith Allah hath provided you, those who disbelieve say unto those who believe: Shall we feed those whom Allah, if He willed, would feed? Ye are in naught else than error manifest

36:48.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
36:48.en: And they say: When will this promise be fulfilled, if ye are truthful

36:49.ar: مَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ تَأۡخُذُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ يَخِصِّمُونَ
36:49.en: They await but one Shout, which will surprise them while they are disputing

36:50.ar: فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ تَوۡصِيَةࣰ وَلَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
36:50.en: Then they cannot make bequest, nor can they return to their own folk

36:51.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَإِذَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَنسِلُونَ
36:51.en: And the trumpet is blown and lo! from the graves they hie unto their Lord

36:52.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰوَيۡلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرۡقَدِنَاۜۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:52.en: Crying: Woe upon us! Who hath raised us from our place of sleep? This is that which the Beneficent did promise, and the messengers spoke truth

36:53.ar: إِن كَانَتۡ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:53.en: It is but one Shout, and behold them brought together before Us

36:54.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
36:54.en: This day no soul is wronged in aught; nor are ye requited aught save what ye used to do

103:2.en: Lo! man is a state of loss

103:3.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ
103:3.en: Save those who believe and do good works, and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance

68:17.ar: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
68:17.en: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning

68:18.en: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah)

68:19.ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
68:19.en: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

68:20.en: And in the morning it was as if plucked

7:187.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَىٰهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّيۖ لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقۡتِهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا تَأۡتِيكُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةࣰۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنۡهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:187.en: They ask thee of the (destined) Hour, when will it come to port. Say: Knowledge thereof is with my Lord only. He alone will manifest it at its proper time. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It cometh not to you save unawares. They question thee as if thou couldst be well informed thereof. Say: Knowledge thereof is with Allah only, but most of mankind know not

h11cbEZ9VWw.speaker: adnan
h11cbEZ9VWw.speaker_note: continues his own Yasin series; speaks of his oncology clinic and growing up in Syria
h11cbEZ9VWw.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 5 (45-54)
h11cbEZ9VWw.one_line: The opposite of a living heart: refusing to learn from past and future, refusing to give, and asking when the Hour comes instead of preparing.
h11cbEZ9VWw.summary: He returns to the surah's theme that obedience to Allah gives life its quality, since we spend far more time dead than alive and the young companions are still remembered. After showing how a heart comes alive, the verses now show its opposite through two refusals. First, when told to beware of what lies before and behind them, people turn away: they will not learn from history, their own past or others' mistakes, the frustration every parent feels when a child repeats their error. From his oncology clinic he describes how people face death according to how they lived, since religion held as mere culture does not help them then, and he urges an honest yearly audit in Ramadan. Second, told to spend, they ask why they should feed someone Allah could have fed. He calls a life without the joy of giving no life at all: inequality exists so that people can give life to others, we are only trustees of what we hold, and the owners of the burnt garden learned this. From his own Syrian past he admits how easily the comfortable ignore the suffering of others. Finally, asking when the promise will come is the wrong question; the Prophet asked what you have prepared. He describes the sudden blast, the resurrection and a judgment where no soul is wronged.

outline.heading: Submission as the source of true life
outline.gist: Yasin looks at submission from the inside: taking the deen into your heart is what makes you truly alive.

outline.heading: Quality of life and the believer's legacy
outline.gist: The Quran defines the piece of quality of life medicine misses: purpose; the young believer of the township lived better than most.

outline.heading: We spend more time dead than alive
outline.gist: Against billions of years, a lifetime barely counts, so the Quran never cares about quantity, only how you lived.

outline.heading: Companions who died young are still remembered
outline.gist: The Prophet, shown a beautiful garment, said the handkerchiefs of a companion who had died years earlier were finer in paradise.

outline.heading: From how to gain life to its opposite
outline.gist: Having shown that iman comes from observing life, the universe and history, Allah now gives two examples of the opposite.

outline.heading: Beware of what is before you and behind you
outline.gist: The disbelievers are told to be mindful; the phrase refers to the future and the past.

outline.heading: Learning from your own past and from earlier nations
outline.gist: Whether read as their own lives or the history of nations, the point is reflecting so as not to repeat harm.

outline.heading: Why parents get upset when children repeat their mistakes
outline.gist: Life is too short to walk a path someone already found worthless; that is what makes parents angry.

outline.heading: So that you may receive mercy: the ego that will not learn
outline.gist: Reflection raises the quality of life, but our sense of being unique stops us from learning from others.

outline.heading: By time: advising one another
outline.gist: Surat al-Asr: we win back time by advising each other about what is worth living and dying for.

outline.heading: The omitted answer: they turn away
outline.gist: Arabic drops what context makes obvious; the sentence is completed by the next verse's turning away.

outline.heading: Every sign ignored: facing death in the clinic
outline.gist: Seeing others die with regret is a sign; in his oncology clinic people face mortality abruptly and react according to how they lived.

outline.heading: Religion as culture does not help at death
outline.gist: When the deen was only a cultural extra, it does not kick in when death comes; what comes out is the sum of how you lived.

outline.heading: Audit your year in Ramadan; it will not just click later
outline.gist: Ask whether last year is worth repeating; graduating, marrying or a new job will not change the essence of your life.

outline.heading: Shall we feed those Allah could have fed?
outline.gist: Told to spend from whatever Allah gave them, wealth, knowledge or time, they argue Allah could feed the poor Himself.

outline.heading: A life without the joy of giving is not worth living
outline.gist: A life centred on consuming is not real life; real life includes the joy of bringing a smile to someone in need.

outline.heading: Unequal hands so we can give each other life
outline.gist: People are dealt different hands so that those who have can find life by sustaining, teaching and protecting others.

outline.heading: Consumerism romanticized
outline.gist: Individual consumption has never been so glorified, perhaps like the spoiled nations Allah punished.

outline.heading: You are only entrusted with it
outline.gist: Land outlives all its owners; the question is whether you give on your own terms before it is taken.

outline.heading: The owners of the garden
outline.gist: Sons of a generous father planned to harvest secretly to avoid the poor, and Allah burnt the garden to the ground.

outline.heading: It is easy to say not my problem when you are fine
outline.gist: The comfortable ignore the oppressed and would feel very differently in their place.

outline.heading: His Syrian experience of indifference
outline.gist: Comfortable Syrians ignored their suffering neighbours, then expected the world to care once they were under fire.

outline.heading: He loves me, look what He gave me: figurative death
outline.gist: Reading wealth as proof of Allah's love and poverty as His choice is being alive without living.

outline.heading: Reading notes: merged letters and the pause
outline.gist: He explains the merged letters in yakhissimun and the brief pause marked in verse 52 that keeps the meaning from running together.

outline.heading: When is this promise? The wrong question
outline.gist: The Prophet answered a man asking when the Hour is with what have you prepared for it; only Allah knows its time.

outline.heading: One blast while they dispute
outline.gist: All they await is a single cry that takes them in the middle of their quarrels over the world.

outline.heading: The Hour strikes in the middle of ordinary life
outline.gist: A man repairing his basin, a morsel that never reaches the mouth, a garment spread between two who never finish the sale.

outline.heading: No will, no return to their families
outline.gist: No time to say goodbye, make amends or tell loved ones they love them.

outline.heading: Only Allah remains
outline.gist: The angel of death takes the last lives and his own; existence is a fragile moment and it was always only Allah.

outline.heading: The second blast: drawn out like threads from a tangle
outline.gist: People are pulled from their graves in perfect order, each body and fingerprint restored, each nation in its place.

outline.heading: Who raised us from our sleeping place?
outline.gist: The first blast ends all existence, like dreamless sleep; those not expecting a second chapter are shocked, and all are brought together.

outline.heading: No soul will be wronged
outline.gist: Each will be judged fairly by the hand they were dealt, their circumstances and their choices.

outline.heading: Not when, but are you ready?
outline.gist: None of it will be your choice when it comes, so prepare now for the life that continues.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Quality, not length, defines a life; the young companions still live through their legacy.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Reflect on your own past and others' mistakes instead of assuming you are unique.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: People face death according to how they lived; audit your life every Ramadan.

themes.label: Parenting and raising children
themes.note: Parents' anger at children repeating their mistakes comes from knowing how short life is.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: A life without the joy of giving is not worth living; we are trustees, as the owners of the garden learned.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: The comfortable ignore the oppressed; his own Syrian community did the same.

themes.label: Syria
themes.note: Syrians' past indifference to suffering neighbours, then the reversal.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The blasts of the horn, resurrection and fair judgment; ask what you have prepared, not when.

quran.point: Humanity is in loss except those who advise one another; learning from others wins back time.
The owners of the garden who planned to deny the poor and found it burnt.
Knowledge of the Hour is with Allah alone and it comes suddenly.

hadith.gist: Shown a fine garment sent as a gift by a king, the Prophet said a deceased companion's handkerchiefs in paradise are better than it (the narration concerns Sa'd ibn Mu'adh).
A man asked when the Hour is; the Prophet replied, what have you prepared for it?
The Hour will come while a man is repairing his basin, another lifting a morsel to his mouth, and two men spreading a garment they will never finish trading.
After the first blast only a few remain; the angel of death is commanded to take their lives and finally his own.

maxims: We're just dead people who haven't died yet
Allah is never interested in quantity
A life without the joy of giving isn't worth living
You're not the owner, you're entrusted
Not when it happens, but are you ready

stories.who: Patients receiving an incurable diagnosis in his clinic
stories.point: People meet death with calm or shock depending on how they lived, not on religion held as culture.

stories.who: The owners of the garden
stories.point: Withholding from the poor what a generous father gave brings ruin.

stories.who: Syrians before and after the war
stories.point: The comfortable ignore others' oppression until they suffer it themselves.

stories.who: The Bedouin asking about the Hour
stories.point: Ask what you have prepared, not when it will come.

contemporary: Oncology care and median-survival conversations
Consumerism and romanticized individual consumption
Palestine under occupation and Iraqi refugees in Syria
Dictatorship and people without passports or freedom of movement
takeaways: Learn from your own past and other people's mistakes instead of repeating them.
Use Ramadan each year to ask honestly whether your last year is worth repeating.
Find joy in giving wealth, time and knowledge, knowing you are only a trustee.
Do not ignore the oppressed just because you are comfortable.
Prepare for the Hour rather than asking when it will be.

18:65.ar: فَوَجَدَا عَبۡدࣰ ا مِّنۡ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمۡنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلۡمࣰ ا
18:65.en: Then found they one of Our slaves, unto whom We had given mercy from Us, and had taught him knowledge from Our presence

18:66.ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلۡ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمۡتَ رُشۡدࣰ ا
18:66.en: Moses said unto him: May I follow thee, to the end that thou mayst teach me right conduct of that which thou hast been taught

18:67.ar: قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبۡرࣰ ا
18:67.en: He said: Lo! thou canst not bear with me

18:68.ar: وَكَيۡفَ تَصۡبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمۡ تُحِطۡ بِهِۦ خُبۡرࣰ ا
18:68.en: How canst thou bear with that whereof thou canst not compass any knowledge

18:69.ar: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرࣰ ا وَلَآ أَعۡصِي لَكَ أَمۡرࣰ ا
18:69.en: He said: Allah willing, thou shalt find me patient and I shall not in aught gainsay thee

18:70.ar: قَالَ فَإِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتَنِي فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِي عَن شَيۡءٍ حَتَّىٰٓ أُحۡدِثَ لَكَ مِنۡهُ ذِكۡرࣰ ا
18:70.en: He said: Well, if thou go with me, ask me not concerning aught till I myself make mention of it unto thee

18:71.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِي ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَاۖ قَالَ أَخَرَقۡتَهَا لِتُغۡرِقَ أَهۡلَهَا لَقَدۡ جِئۡتَ شَيۡـًٔا إِمۡرࣰ ا
18:71.en: So they twain set out till, when they were in the ship, he made a hole therein. (Moses) said: Hast thou made a hole therein to drown the folk thereof? Thou verily hast done a dreadful thing

18:72.ar: قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُلۡ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبۡرࣰ ا
18:72.en: He said: Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me

18:73.ar: قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرۡهِقۡنِي مِنۡ أَمۡرِي عُسۡرࣰ ا
18:73.en: (Moses) said: Be not wroth with me that I forgot, and be not hard upon me for my fault

18:74.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَٰمࣰ ا فَقَتَلَهُۥ قَالَ أَقَتَلۡتَ نَفۡسࣰ ا زَكِيَّةَۢ بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسࣲ لَّقَدۡ جِئۡتَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا نُّكۡرࣰ ا
18:74.en: So they twain journeyed on till, when they met a lad, he slew him. (Moses) said: What! Hast thou slain an innocent soul who hath slain no man? Verily thou hast done a horrid thing

18:75.ar: ۞قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبۡرࣰ ا
18:75.en: He said: Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me

18:76.ar: قَالَ إِن سَأَلۡتُكَ عَن شَيۡءِۭ بَعۡدَهَا فَلَا تُصَٰحِبۡنِيۖ قَدۡ بَلَغۡتَ مِن لَّدُنِّي عُذۡرࣰ ا
18:76.en: (Moses) said: If I ask thee after this concerning aught, keep not company with me. Thou hast received an excuse from me

18:77.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهۡلَ قَرۡيَةٍ ٱسۡتَطۡعَمَآ أَهۡلَهَا فَأَبَوۡاْ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارࣰ ا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥۖ قَالَ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ لَتَّخَذۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرࣰ ا
18:77.en: So they twain journeyed on till, when they came unto the folk of a certain township, they asked its folk for food, but they refused to make them guests. And they found therein a wall upon the point of falling into ruin, and he repaired it. (Moses) said: If thou hadst wished, thou couldst have taken payment for it

18:78.ar: قَالَ هَٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنِكَۚ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأۡوِيلِ مَا لَمۡ تَسۡتَطِع عَّلَيۡهِ صَبۡرًا
18:78.en: He said: This is the parting between thee and me! I will announce unto thee the interpretation of that thou couldst not bear with patience

18:79.ar: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتۡ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكࣱ يَأۡخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصۡبࣰ ا
18:79.en: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working on the river, and I wished to mar it, for there was a king behind them who is taking every ship by force

18:80.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡغُلَٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤۡمِنَيۡنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرۡهِقَهُمَا طُغۡيَٰنࣰ ا وَكُفۡرࣰ ا
18:80.en: And as for the lad, his parents were believers and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief

18:81.ar: فَأَرَدۡنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُ زَكَوٰةࣰ وَأَقۡرَبَ رُحۡمࣰ ا
18:81.en: And we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in purity and nearer to mercy

18:82.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَٰمَيۡنِ يَتِيمَيۡنِ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحۡتَهُۥ كَنزࣱ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبۡلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسۡتَخۡرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَۚ وَمَا فَعَلۡتُهُۥ عَنۡ أَمۡرِيۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَأۡوِيلُ مَا لَمۡ تَسۡطِع عَّلَيۡهِ صَبۡرࣰ ا
18:82.en: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous, and thy Lord intended that they should come to their full strength and should bring forth their treasure as a mercy from their Lord; and I did it not upon my own command. Such is the interpretation of that wherewith thou couldst not bear

19:42.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعۡبُدُ مَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ وَلَا يُبۡصِرُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي عَنكَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:42.en: When he said unto his father: O my father! Why worshippest thou that which heareth not nor seeth, nor can in aught avail thee

19:43.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي قَدۡ جَآءَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مَا لَمۡ يَأۡتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعۡنِيٓ أَهۡدِكَ صِرَٰطࣰ ا سَوِيࣰّ ا
19:43.en: O my father! Lo! there hath come unto me of knowledge that which came not unto thee. So follow me, and I will lead thee on a right path

19:44.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعۡبُدِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ عَصِيࣰّ ا
19:44.en: O my father! Serve not the devil. Lo! the devil is a rebel unto the Beneficent

19:45.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابࣱ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيࣰّ ا
19:45.en: O my father! Lo! I fear lest a punishment from the Beneficent overtake thee so that thou become a comrade of the devil

19:46.ar: قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنۡ ءَالِهَتِي يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ لَأَرۡجُمَنَّكَۖ وَٱهۡجُرۡنِي مَلِيࣰّ ا
19:46.en: He said: Rejectest thou my gods, O Abraham? If thou cease not, I shall surely stone thee. Depart from me a long while

19:47.ar: قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكَۖ سَأَسۡتَغۡفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّيٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِي حَفِيࣰّ ا
19:47.en: He said: Peace be unto thee! I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for thee. Lo! He was ever gracious unto me

20:43.en: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds)

20:44.ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا لَّيِّنࣰ ا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ
20:44.en: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear

4:94.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا ضَرَبۡتُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُواْ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلسَّلَٰمَ لَسۡتَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا تَبۡتَغُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ كَثِيرَةࣱۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلُ فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:94.en: O ye who believe! When ye go forth (to fight) in the way of Allah, be careful to discriminate, and say not unto one who offereth you peace: "Thou art not a believer," seeking the chance profits of this life (so that ye may despoil him). With Allah are plenteous spoils. Even thus (as he now is) were ye before; but Allah hath since then been gracious unto you. Therefore take care to discriminate. Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

9:114.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱسۡتِغۡفَارُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَن مَّوۡعِدَةࣲ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥٓ أَنَّهُۥ عَدُوࣱّ لِّلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُۚ إِنَّ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لَأَوَّٰهٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
9:114.en: The prayer of Abraham for the forgiveness of his father was only because of a promise he had promised him, but when it had become clear unto him that he (his father) was an enemy to Allah he (Abraham) disowned him. Lo! Abraham was soft of heart, long-suffering

17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

79:24.en: And proclaimed: "I (Pharaoh) am your Lord the Highest

HIEPYw5pIKY.speaker: adnan
HIEPYw5pIKY.speaker_note: Sh. Adnan's Ramadan halqa series; recalls his village teacher in Syria and the greeting team at Muslim Wellness Network
HIEPYw5pIKY.title: Soft Speech (Ramadan 2026, Night 15: Quranic Themes 2)
HIEPYw5pIKY.one_line: Why the Quran calls for soft speech, shown through al-Khidr with Musa, Ibrahim with his father, and Musa and Harun sent gently to Pharaoh.
HIEPYw5pIKY.summary: Soft speech, he explains, appears in the Quran both as a command and in how prophets addressed even hostile people. It is not weakness or a lack of assertiveness; it is the caller's duty to remove obstacles, because harsh delivery forces listeners to fight their ego as well as the message and puts them on the defensive. He tells of a gentle teacher in his village whose talks on love only reached rough farmers once he spoke about hellfire, showing audiences differ, yet softness generally works, and guidance is Allah's gift, not a license to judge. Al-Khidr, after Musa broke his promise three times, parted from him gently and still explained everything, because he had been given mercy before knowledge; knowledge without mercy produces the destruction seen on today's screens. Ibrahim called his idol-worshipping father by a tender name, said he feared for him, and answered threats of stoning with peace and prayers for forgiveness, consistently. Young people should therefore never be harsh with parents, not even say 'uff', and should serve rather than correct them. Finally, Allah told Musa and Harun to speak gently to Pharaoh, the worst tyrant, so his ego would not block him. Masajid exist to serve and welcome people, and the only goal is hearts finding Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Soft speech: command and prophetic example
outline.gist: Allah commands soft speech and the prophets used it with tyrants and enemies; it does not mean lacking assertiveness or letting people walk over you.

outline.heading: Do not give people two obstacles
outline.gist: Harsh speech makes people both accept the message and overcome their ego; whoever calls to Allah must lessen the obstacles between people and the truth.

outline.heading: The speaker does the most work
outline.gist: No one enjoys being lectured, so the speaker's job is to do as much work as possible so the listener does as little as possible.

outline.heading: Tone decides whether people get defensive
outline.gist: Beyond sound content and timing, tone matters: an aggressive delivery provokes pushback and justification, while a soft one leaves only the discomfort of being wrong. The scholars he learned from were all soft-spoken.

outline.heading: His gentle teacher in the village
outline.gist: A tender teacher's talks on love did not reach the rough farmers of his village; when he finally gave a khutbah on hellfire in 2003 the masjid overflowed the next morning, so audiences differ, though softness generally works.

outline.heading: Guidance is a gift, not a license to be harsh
outline.gist: We are guided only by Allah's generosity, so it is bad manners to judge or be harsh with those whose hearts have not yet opened; even in war the Quran says you were once lost too.

outline.heading: Musa learns someone knows more
outline.gist: After Musa told Bani Israel no one knew more than him, he learned of a more knowledgeable servant and set out to learn, because prophets seek knowledge wherever it is found.

outline.heading: 'You will not be able to bear with me'
outline.gist: The Quran calls him only a servant of Allah; he sees him as the decree of Allah in action, and he warns Musa that he will not understand his actions.

outline.heading: Musa insists on companionship
outline.gist: Musa wanted to accompany him, not just ask questions; the condition was not to ask until told. No ordinary human, sheikh or otherwise, may ask for such blind following.

outline.heading: The ship and the boy
outline.gist: Musa objected every time: when the servant holed a poor family's ship, and when he took a child's life, apologising after each protest.

outline.heading: Rebuilding a wall for a stingy village
outline.gist: The village refused them the customary hospitality, yet the servant rebuilt a collapsing wall, heavy labour, and Musa objected a third time.

outline.heading: 'This is the parting between us'
outline.gist: After Musa broke his word three times, the servant could have been harsh but simply and gently said they must part ways.

outline.heading: The explanations
outline.gist: The hole saved the ship from a king seizing sound vessels, the boy would have led good parents to disbelief, and the wall protected two orphans' treasure.

outline.heading: What Musa missed
outline.gist: Had he stayed silent he would have seen more of Allah's subtle work behind why one person thrives and another suffers; still, the servant took the time to explain.

outline.heading: Mercy before knowledge
outline.gist: Allah describes the servant as given mercy first and knowledge second, which is why he was gentle and patient; knowledge and technology without mercy produce bombing, genocide and poverty.

outline.heading: Watching the world burn on split screens
outline.gist: Past brutality was not broadcast; now we watch cities burning on divided screens and must find ways to cope with this needless show of dominance.

outline.heading: How Ibrahim spoke to his father
outline.gist: The passage is chosen for the way Ibrahim addressed his father.

outline.heading: 'Ya abati': the tender form
outline.gist: Changing a letter in Arabic makes a word more affectionate, as when the Prophet shortened Aisha's name; Ibrahim used the tender form of 'my father'.

outline.heading: Interlude
'Why worship what neither hears nor sees?'
outline.gist: Speaking to a leader of his people who was his father or uncle, Ibrahim gives the basic argument and says he is not better, only given knowledge his father had not received.

outline.heading: 'I fear for you'
outline.gist: He warns his father against serving Shaytan and says he fears the slightest touch of Allah's punishment reaching him.

outline.heading: Threatened with stoning, he answers with peace
outline.gist: His father threatens to stone him and drives him out; Ibrahim replies 'peace be upon you' and promises to seek his Lord's forgiveness for him.

outline.heading: Gentle toward a hostile father
outline.gist: Ibrahim was later told not to seek forgiveness for those hostile to the faith, but here, facing abuse and threats of violence, his speech stayed soft.

outline.heading: Most of you have parents who support your faith
outline.gist: Apart from some converts, the more religious you are the prouder your parents are; even parents who forbade Islam would still be owed soft speech.

outline.heading: Before you raise your voice at your parents
outline.gist: Ibrahim offered peace, prayer and to leave when asked; remember him before you yell at or point fingers at your mother or father.

outline.heading: Ibrahim was consistent
outline.gist: The point of the story is that his tone never changed: loving at the start and loving when threatened with death.

outline.heading: Not even 'uff': the weakest sound
outline.gist: If you are not facing what Ibrahim faced, why the anger? Of Arabic letters the fa has no feature of strength, and 'uff' is barely a word, yet even it is forbidden toward parents.

outline.heading: You are not here to correct your parents
outline.gist: Young people who catch parents in mistakes should not become self-righteous: even a prophet approached his father emotionally, not by saying 'you are wrong'. Your job is to serve them, change yourself, and be thankful.

outline.heading: Sent to the worst tyrant
outline.gist: Pharaoh enslaved a whole people, deemed them less human and declared himself the highest lord.

outline.heading: 'Speak to him gently'
outline.gist: One would expect a forceful approach backed by Allah's power, yet Musa and Harun were told to speak softly so he might remember or feel reverence.

outline.heading: Removing the ego obstacle, even for Pharaoh
outline.gist: Soft speech left Pharaoh only his own self-deception to deal with, bringing him a step closer to God; he still refused, but the caller's part is done.

outline.heading: Masajid are here to serve
outline.gist: Masajid are not countries and Muslim institutions are not governments; their only purpose is to serve and to make the way in easier, never intimidating.

outline.heading: Greet the newcomer
outline.gist: He prayed for nine years beside people whose names he never learned; at Wellness they arranged for people to greet anyone they see for the first time.

outline.heading: The goal is hearts finding Allah
outline.gist: If harshness was ever acceptable it was with Pharaoh, yet softness was commanded; we may be accountable for making it hard for people, and the only objective is drawing hearts to Allah.

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

2:273.ar: لِلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحۡصِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ ضَرۡبࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَحۡسَبُهُمُ ٱلۡجَاهِلُ أَغۡنِيَآءَ مِنَ ٱلتَّعَفُّفِ تَعۡرِفُهُم بِسِيمَٰهُمۡ لَا يَسۡـَٔلُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ إِلۡحَافࣰ اۗ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِۦ عَلِيمٌ
2:273.en: (Alms are) for the poor who are straitened for the cause of Allah, who cannot travel in the land (for trade). The unthinking man accounteth them wealthy because of their restraint. Thou shalt know them by their mark: They do not beg of men with importunity. And whatsoever good thing ye spend, lo! Allah knoweth it

24:33.ar: وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ اۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنࣰ ا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِكۡرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:33.en: And let those who cannot find a match keep chaste till Allah give them independence by His grace. And such of your slaves as seek a writing (of emancipation), write it for them if ye are aware of aught of good in them, and bestow upon them of the wealth of Allah which He hath bestowed upon you. Force not your slave-girls to whoredom that ye may seek enjoyment of the life of the world, if they would preserve their chastity. And if one force them, then (unto them), after their compulsion, lo! Allah will be Forgiving, Merciful

ElFKMWEm4io.speaker: adnan
ElFKMWEm4io.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan values series with two values each morning
ElFKMWEm4io.title: The Values of Islam: Haya (Moral Awareness and Sensitivity) and 'Iffah (Restraint and Chastity)
ElFKMWEm4io.one_line: Haya is not shyness but moral awareness and sensitivity, the one value with no upper limit; 'iffah is the restraint that refuses to cheapen oneself.
ElFKMWEm4io.summary: The sheikh argues that translating haya as modesty or shyness shrinks it. It is moral awareness and sensitivity: knowing oneself and one's surroundings and responding to them. He gathers prophetic narrations: 'if you have no haya, do as you wish', haya brings only good, it is a branch of eman, and it is Islam's defining character. Linguistically haya comes from the root of life, so it is life at its height; the dead are defined by not responding, and the elderly lose filters as awareness fades. Unlike every other value, which turns harmful when pushed too far, haya has no limit, which is why the Prophet emphasised it so often and was more sensitive than a secluded maiden. Haya produces modest dress and lowered gaze for both men and women, without demanding weakness from strong, confident women, and its absence shows in people who barge in, block entrances or run stop signs. 'Iffah is not repression but restraint over how appetites for wealth, sex and power are pursued, the law that keeps desire's marketplace from swallowing the city, as advertising does today. It is the refusal to cheapen oneself, seen in the poor who never beg, the unmarried who stay chaste, and the opposite of the boss's flatterer. Dignity, he concludes, is not a value but the result of these two.

outline.heading: Haya cannot be translated
outline.gist: Rendering haya as modesty reduces the concept and drains its meaning.

outline.heading: Moral awareness and sensitivity
outline.gist: Haya is not toxic shame, guilt or humiliation but moral elegance: awareness of self and surroundings.

outline.heading: A teaching from early prophethood
outline.gist: If you have no haya, do as you wish: without it there is no restraint at all.

outline.heading: Haya brings only good
outline.gist: Said to a man rebuking his brother for it; haya is also a branch of eman.

outline.heading: Islam's defining character
outline.gist: Every religion has a defining trait and Islam's is haya; the slang sense of shyness causes confusion.

outline.heading: Shyness is a behaviour, haya a value
outline.gist: Depending on the situation haya may produce shyness or even loudness.

outline.heading: Haya as the height of life
outline.gist: The Arabic pattern makes haya the highest manifestation of hayat, life.

outline.heading: The dead do not respond
outline.gist: Death is a lack of response; the more aware a living being is, the more alive.

outline.heading: Losing filters with age
outline.gist: Elderly relatives who say anything show fading awareness; haya becomes consideration.

outline.heading: Every value is governed and limited
outline.gist: Truth, justice and moral absolutism rank the values, and moderation applies each one.

outline.heading: Too much of a value becomes a problem
outline.gist: Generosity, for example, can harm one's family when pushed too far.

outline.heading: The one value with no limit
outline.gist: The Prophet repeated haya so often because with it, the more the better.

outline.heading: More sensitive than a secluded maiden
outline.gist: Other values flip into their opposites; the Prophet's awareness was heightened all his life.

outline.heading: Why haya becomes modesty
outline.gist: Awareness of oneself and others translates into how one dresses and behaves, as with the Prophet's haya toward Uthman.

outline.heading: Men lowering the gaze
outline.gist: Aware of women around him, a man lowers his gaze literally and figuratively and dresses respectfully.

outline.heading: Strong women with haya
outline.gist: Haya does not mean weakness; aware women dress and carry themselves mindful of how society works.

outline.heading: People who barge in
outline.gist: Without awareness people are loud and clumsy; the aware person scans the room for what would bother others.

outline.heading: Big trucks and stop signs
outline.gist: Living as if no one else exists is not evil but a loss of moral awareness.

outline.heading: A society of considerate people
outline.gist: A masjid and society full of haya respects space and privacy and rises.

outline.heading: 'Iffah: the poor thought to be rich
outline.gist: Allah describes needy people whose restraint makes the unaware think them wealthy.

outline.heading: Restraint, not repression
outline.gist: Islam recognises appetites; 'iffah is the law that governs desire's marketplace.

outline.heading: When the marketplace swallows the city
outline.gist: Advertising during a football game sells everything with bodies because nothing restrains it.

outline.heading: Refusing to cheapen oneself
outline.gist: Haya and 'iffah together protect human dignity.

outline.heading: Losing dignity through carelessness
outline.gist: Running an intersection invites deserved insult; those unable to marry must keep chaste.

outline.heading: Zina sells the self cheaply
outline.gist: Falling into what Allah saw as beneath you sells your own dignity.

outline.heading: Restraint more valuable than wealth
outline.gist: The poor who refuse to beg keep their dignity; a Muslim sells himself for nothing.

outline.heading: The boss's pet
outline.gist: Flattering superiors for advancement sells dignity, and a person with haya will not accept it either.

outline.heading: Etiquette versus selling dignity
outline.gist: Good manners are different from trading dignity for sex, wealth or status.

outline.heading: Dignity is a result, not a value
outline.gist: Practise haya and 'iffah and dignity follows throughout life.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)

themes.label: Modernity, secularism, materialism and their effects
themes.note: Advertising that sells everything through bodies.

themes.note: Dignity as the fruit of refusing to sell oneself cheaply.

33:72.ar: إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَهَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡهَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومࣰ ا جَهُولࣰ ا
33:72.en: Lo! We offered the trust unto the heavens and the earth and the hills, but they shrank from bearing it and were afraid of it. And man assumed it. Lo! he hath proved a tyrant and a fool

76:30.ar: وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
76:30.en: Yet ye will not, unless Allah willeth. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

36:20.en: And there came from the uttermost part of the city a man running. He cried: O my people! Follow those who have been sent

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him)? Will ye not then heed

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son)

K5-qQFsxlrA.speaker: adnan
K5-qQFsxlrA.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan values series, recapping his earlier lessons on stewardship and service
K5-qQFsxlrA.title: The Values of Islam: Hurriyyah (Freedom) and Shaja'ah (Courage)
K5-qQFsxlrA.one_line: Freedom of will is the trust humans carried and courage is what makes it real; both need the pursuit of truth, and fear, desire, oppression and bigotry destroy them.
K5-qQFsxlrA.summary: The sheikh pairs freedom and courage as values a steward and servant needs. The trust offered to the heavens, earth and mountains was free will, and true servanthood to Allah requires a free choice; one reason the Arabs carried the final message was their untamed freedom. Courage is not the absence of fear but refusing to let fear decide, and each brave act rewires avoidance, as with exposure therapy and Ibn Mas'ud reciting publicly three days running. Freedom without courage is empty: widespread timidity breeds tyranny. Yet freedom without moral direction becomes chaos, as the West reduced a profound value to licence, and courage for the wrong side is still a problem, so both must be governed by the pursuit of truth. Four things steal freedom: fear, enslavement to desires, external oppression, which leaves the will free as with Bilal, and bigotry or agenda-driven thinking. Muslims follow Islam because it is true, as in the verse offering to worship a son of the Most Merciful if one were proven. He warns against teachers who bend texts to defend a school, says his teachers taught him to argue with them, rejects blind obedience outside battlefield orders, and urges Muslims in the West to escape the financial and social chains that silence them.

outline.heading: Why freedom and courage come next
outline.gist: A steward who serves selflessly needs a measure of freedom and courage.

outline.heading: The trust is free will
outline.gist: The heavens, earth and mountains refused the trust out of fear; humans carried it, and servanthood needs free choice.

outline.heading: Why the Arabs were chosen
outline.gist: Spared foreign empires because the desert held nothing worth conquering, they kept a freedom no one could coerce.

outline.heading: Courage needs fear
outline.gist: Batman is brave and Superman is not; the believers feel fear but do not show it.

outline.heading: Bravery rewires avoidance
outline.gist: Like exposure therapy, each brave act weakens the fear circuit, as with the man who ran to warn his city.

outline.heading: Ibn Mas'ud recites in public
outline.gist: Beaten for reciting the Quran before the Quraysh, he returned and said he had never feared them less.

outline.heading: Timidity breeds tyranny
outline.gist: Freedom unused out of fear is not freedom; democracies depend on civic courage.

outline.heading: Freedom without moral direction
outline.gist: The West built itself on freedom but reduced it to the freedom to offend and expose.

outline.heading: Courage on the wrong side
outline.gist: Bravery for a wrong cause is still bravery but not praiseworthy.

outline.heading: Value, principle and governing ethic
outline.gist: Freedom is the value, speaking my mind the principle, and the pursuit of truth must govern both.

outline.heading: Freedom killer one: fear
outline.gist: Most of the time it is fear of losing something that holds back freedom.

outline.heading: Freedom killer two: desires
outline.gist: One enslaved by greed for wealth, status or sex has a free body but a coerced will, taking desire as a god.

outline.heading: Freedom killer three: oppression
outline.gist: Bodily enslavement is lesser, since the will stays free, as with the early Muslim slaves.

outline.heading: Bilal, freer than us
outline.gist: The Quran treats slavery as an evil to remove, but Bilal's will defeated his owners.

outline.heading: Freedom killer four: bigotry
outline.gist: I am not right because I follow Islam; I follow Islam because it is right.

outline.heading: If the Most Merciful had a son
outline.gist: The Quran's offer to follow proof wherever it leads shows a faith built on freely pursued truth.

outline.heading: Cults and agendas
outline.gist: Anything you may not question, whether party, nationalism or racism, limits your freedom of thought.

outline.heading: Truth as the governing ethic
outline.gist: Without it freedom becomes chaos and bravery recklessness; objectivity requires freedom.

outline.heading: Do not trust a teacher with an agenda
outline.gist: A speaker who bends texts to defend a scholar or school cannot be trusted; his teachers taught him to argue with them.

outline.heading: Adab is not blind following
outline.gist: Respect scholars but never follow an opinion you think wrong; honest mistakes differ from systematic ones.

outline.heading: No blind following, not even of the Prophet
outline.gist: He brought arguments; only operational orders in a war already judged righteous are followed without debate.

outline.heading: The mindless soldier has no excuse
outline.gist: Even an enslaved body keeps the choice not to harm and is accountable for it.

outline.heading: Enslaved by mortgages and status
outline.gist: People today stay silent at wrongs for fear of losing jobs and payments.

outline.heading: Become free again
outline.gist: Bilal had nothing left to lose; Muslims in the West must free themselves to speak and pursue truth rather than safety.

themes.label: Modernity, secularism, materialism and their effects

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies

19:2.en: A mention of the mercy of thy Lord unto His servant Zachariah

19:3.ar: إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ نِدَآءً خَفِيࣰّ ا
19:3.en: When he cried unto his Lord a cry in secret

19:4.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ ٱلۡعَظۡمُ مِنِّي وَٱشۡتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأۡسُ شَيۡبࣰ ا وَلَمۡ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيࣰّ ا
19:4.en: Saying: My Lord! Lo! the bones of me wax feeble and my head is shining with grey hair, and I have never been unblest in prayer to Thee, my Lord

19:5.ar: وَإِنِّي خِفۡتُ ٱلۡمَوَٰلِيَ مِن وَرَآءِي وَكَانَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتِي عَاقِرࣰ ا فَهَبۡ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيࣰّ ا
19:5.en: Lo! I fear my kinsfolk after me, since my wife is barren. Oh, give me from Thy presence a successor

19:6.ar: يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنۡ ءَالِ يَعۡقُوبَۖ وَٱجۡعَلۡهُ رَبِّ رَضِيࣰّ ا
19:6.en: Who shall inherit of me and inherit (also) of the house of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, acceptable (unto Thee)

19:7.ar: يَٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ ٱسۡمُهُۥ يَحۡيَىٰ لَمۡ نَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُ سَمِيࣰّ ا
19:7.en: (It was said unto him): O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son whose name is John; we have given the same name to none before (him)

19:8.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَٰمࣱ وَكَانَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتِي عَاقِرࣰ ا وَقَدۡ بَلَغۡتُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِبَرِ عِتِيࣰّ ا
19:8.en: He said: My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached infirm old age

19:9.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنࣱ وَقَدۡ خَلَقۡتُكَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَلَمۡ تَكُ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:9.en: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me, even as I created thee before, when thou wast naught

19:10.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَل لِّيٓ ءَايَةࣰۖ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَ لَيَالࣲ سَوِيࣰّ ا
19:10.en: He said: My Lord! Appoint for me some token. He said: Thy token is that thou, with no bodily defect, shalt not speak unto mankind three nights

19:11.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابِ فَأَوۡحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ أَن سَبِّحُواْ بُكۡرَةࣰ وَعَشِيࣰّ ا
19:11.en: Then he came forth unto his people from the sanctuary, and signified to them: Glorify your Lord at break of day and fall of night

19:12.ar: يَٰيَحۡيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِقُوَّةࣲۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمَ صَبِيࣰّ ا
19:12.en: (And it was said unto his son): O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom when a child

19:13.ar: وَحَنَانࣰ ا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَوٰةࣰۖ وَكَانَ تَقِيࣰّ ا
19:13.en: And compassion from Our presence, and purity; and he was devout

19:14.ar: وَبَرَّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيࣰّ ا
19:14.en: And dutiful toward his parents. And he was not arrogant, rebellious

19:15.ar: وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡهِ يَوۡمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوۡمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوۡمَ يُبۡعَثُ حَيࣰّ ا
19:15.en: Peace on him the day he was born, and the day he dieth and the day he shall be raised alive

19:16.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَرۡيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتۡ مِنۡ أَهۡلِهَا مَكَانࣰ ا شَرۡقِيࣰّ ا
19:16.en: And make mention of Mary in the Scripture, when she had withdrawn from her people to a chamber looking East

19:17.ar: فَٱتَّخَذَتۡ مِن دُونِهِمۡ حِجَابࣰ ا فَأَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرࣰ ا سَوِيࣰّ ا
19:17.en: And had chosen seclusion from them. Then We sent unto her Our Spirit and it assumed for her the likeness of a perfect man

19:18.ar: قَالَتۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيࣰّ ا
19:18.en: She said: Lo! I seek refuge in the Beneficent One from thee, if thou art Allah-fearing

19:19.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَٰمࣰ ا زَكِيࣰّ ا
19:19.en: He said: I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a faultless son

19:20.ar: قَالَتۡ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَٰمࣱ وَلَمۡ يَمۡسَسۡنِي بَشَرࣱ وَلَمۡ أَكُ بَغِيࣰّ ا
19:20.en: She said: How can I have a son when no mortal hath touched me, neither have I been unchaste

19:21.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنࣱۖ وَلِنَجۡعَلَهُۥٓ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّاۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرࣰ ا مَّقۡضِيࣰّ ا
19:21.en: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me. And (it will be) that We may make of him a revelation for mankind and a mercy from Us, and it is a thing ordained

19:22.ar: ۞فَحَمَلَتۡهُ فَٱنتَبَذَتۡ بِهِۦ مَكَانࣰ ا قَصِيࣰّ ا
19:22.en: And she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place

19:23.ar: فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلۡمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذۡعِ ٱلنَّخۡلَةِ قَالَتۡ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي مِتُّ قَبۡلَ هَٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسۡيࣰ ا مَّنسِيࣰّ ا
19:23.en: And the pangs of childbirth drove her unto the trunk of the palm-tree. She said: Oh, would that I had died ere this and had become a thing of naught, forgotten

19:24.ar: فَنَادَىٰهَا مِن تَحۡتِهَآ أَلَّا تَحۡزَنِي قَدۡ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحۡتَكِ سَرِيࣰّ ا
19:24.en: Then (one) cried unto her from below her, saying: Grieve not! Thy Lord hath placed a rivulet beneath thee

19:25.ar: وَهُزِّيٓ إِلَيۡكِ بِجِذۡعِ ٱلنَّخۡلَةِ تُسَٰقِطۡ عَلَيۡكِ رُطَبࣰ ا جَنِيࣰّ ا
19:25.en: And shake the trunk of the palm-tree toward thee, thou wilt cause ripe dates to fall upon thee

19:26.ar: فَكُلِي وَٱشۡرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيۡنࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡبَشَرِ أَحَدࣰ ا فَقُولِيٓ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ صَوۡمࣰ ا فَلَنۡ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ إِنسِيࣰّ ا
19:26.en: So eat and drink and be consoled. And if thou meetest any mortal, say: Lo! I have vowed a fast unto the Beneficent, and may not speak this day to any mortal

19:27.ar: فَأَتَتۡ بِهِۦ قَوۡمَهَا تَحۡمِلُهُۥۖ قَالُواْ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ لَقَدۡ جِئۡتِ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا فَرِيࣰّ ا
19:27.en: Then she brought him to her own folk, carrying him. They said: O Mary! Thou hast come with an amazing thing

19:28.ar: يَٰٓأُخۡتَ هَٰرُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ ٱمۡرَأَ سَوۡءࣲ وَمَا كَانَتۡ أُمُّكِ بَغِيࣰّ ا
19:28.en: O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a wicked man nor was thy mother a harlot

19:29.ar: فَأَشَارَتۡ إِلَيۡهِۖ قَالُواْ كَيۡفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِي ٱلۡمَهۡدِ صَبِيࣰّ ا
19:29.en: Then she pointed to him. They said: How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy

19:30.ar: قَالَ إِنِّي عَبۡدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِيَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيࣰّ ا
19:30.en: He spake: Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet

19:31.ar: وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكًا أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوۡصَٰنِي بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ مَا دُمۡتُ حَيࣰّ ا
19:31.en: And hath made me blessed wheresoever I may be, and hath enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving so long as I remain alive

19:32.ar: وَبَرَّۢا بِوَٰلِدَتِي وَلَمۡ يَجۡعَلۡنِي جَبَّارࣰ ا شَقِيࣰّ ا
19:32.en: And (hath made me) dutiful toward her who bore me, and hath not made me arrogant, unblest

19:33.ar: وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَيَّ يَوۡمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوۡمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوۡمَ أُبۡعَثُ حَيࣰّ ا
19:33.en: Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive

19:34.ar: ذَٰلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَۖ قَوۡلَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يَمۡتَرُونَ
19:34.en: Such was Jesus, son of Mary: (this is) a statement of the truth concerning which they doubt

19:35.ar: مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدࣲۖ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥٓۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
19:35.en: It befitteth not (the Majesty of) Allah that He should take unto Himself a son. Glory be to Him! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is

19:36.ar: وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمۡ فَٱعۡبُدُوهُۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطࣱ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣱ‏
19:36.en: And lo! Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So serve Him. That is the right path

19:37.ar: فَٱخۡتَلَفَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِهِمۡۖ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن مَّشۡهَدِ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمٍ
19:37.en: The sects among them differ: but woe unto the disbelievers from the meeting of an awful Day

19:38.ar: أَسۡمِعۡ بِهِمۡ وَأَبۡصِرۡ يَوۡمَ يَأۡتُونَنَا لَٰكِنِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
19:38.en: See and hear them on the Day they come unto Us! yet the evil-doers are to-day in error manifest

19:39.ar: وَأَنذِرۡهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحَسۡرَةِ إِذۡ قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ وَهُمۡ فِي غَفۡلَةࣲ وَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
19:39.en: And warn them of the Day of anguish when the case hath been decided. Now they are in a state of carelessness, and they believe not

19:40.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَرِثُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَنۡ عَلَيۡهَا وَإِلَيۡنَا يُرۡجَعُونَ
19:40.en: Lo! We, only We, inherit the earth and all who are thereon, and unto Us they are returned

19:41.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقࣰ ا نَّبِيًّا
19:41.en: And make mention (O Muhammad) in the Scripture of Abraham. Lo! he was a saint, a prophet

19:42.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعۡبُدُ مَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ وَلَا يُبۡصِرُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي عَنكَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:42.en: When he said unto his father: O my father! Why worshippest thou that which heareth not nor seeth, nor can in aught avail thee

19:43.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي قَدۡ جَآءَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مَا لَمۡ يَأۡتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعۡنِيٓ أَهۡدِكَ صِرَٰطࣰ ا سَوِيࣰّ ا
19:43.en: O my father! Lo! there hath come unto me of knowledge that which came not unto thee. So follow me, and I will lead thee on a right path

19:44.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعۡبُدِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ عَصِيࣰّ ا
19:44.en: O my father! Serve not the devil. Lo! the devil is a rebel unto the Beneficent

19:45.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابࣱ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيࣰّ ا
19:45.en: O my father! Lo! I fear lest a punishment from the Beneficent overtake thee so that thou become a comrade of the devil

19:46.ar: قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنۡ ءَالِهَتِي يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ لَأَرۡجُمَنَّكَۖ وَٱهۡجُرۡنِي مَلِيࣰّ ا
19:46.en: He said: Rejectest thou my gods, O Abraham? If thou cease not, I shall surely stone thee. Depart from me a long while

19:47.ar: قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكَۖ سَأَسۡتَغۡفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّيٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِي حَفِيࣰّ ا
19:47.en: He said: Peace be unto thee! I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for thee. Lo! He was ever gracious unto me

19:48.ar: وَأَعۡتَزِلُكُمۡ وَمَا تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَدۡعُواْ رَبِّي عَسَىٰٓ أَلَّآ أَكُونَ بِدُعَآءِ رَبِّي شَقِيࣰّ ا
19:48.en: I shall withdraw from you and that unto which ye pray beside Allah, and I shall pray unto my Lord. It may be that, in prayer unto my Lord, I shall not be unblest

19:49.ar: فَلَمَّا ٱعۡتَزَلَهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَۖ وَكُلࣰّ ا جَعَلۡنَا نَبِيࣰّ ا
19:49.en: So, when he had withdrawn from them and that which they were worshipping beside Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob. Each of them We made a prophet

19:50.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِنَا وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُمۡ لِسَانَ صِدۡقٍ عَلِيࣰّ ا
19:50.en: And we gave them of Our mercy, and assigned to them a high and true renown

19:51.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مُوسَىٰٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مُخۡلَصࣰ ا وَكَانَ رَسُولࣰ ا نَّبِيࣰّ ا
19:51.en: And make mention in the Scripture of Moses. Lo! he was chosen, and he was a messenger (of Allah), a prophet

19:52.ar: وَنَٰدَيۡنَٰهُ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ وَقَرَّبۡنَٰهُ نَجِيࣰّ ا
19:52.en: We called him from the right slope of the Mount, and brought him nigh in communion

19:53.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥ مِن رَّحۡمَتِنَآ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ نَبِيࣰّ ا
19:53.en: And We bestowed upon him of Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet (likewise)

19:54.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صَادِقَ ٱلۡوَعۡدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولࣰ ا نَّبِيࣰّ ا
19:54.en: And make mention in the Scripture of Ishmael. Lo! he was a keeper of his promise, and he was a messenger (of Allah), a prophet

19:55.ar: وَكَانَ يَأۡمُرُ أَهۡلَهُۥ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ مَرۡضِيࣰّ ا
19:55.en: He enjoined upon his people worship and almsgiving, and was acceptable in the sight of his Lord

19:56.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِدۡرِيسَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقࣰ ا نَّبِيࣰّ ا
19:56.en: And make mention in the Scripture of Idris. Lo! he was a saint, a prophet

19:57.en: And We raised him to high station

19:58.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ ءَادَمَ وَمِمَّنۡ حَمَلۡنَا مَعَ نُوحࣲ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّةِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَمِمَّنۡ هَدَيۡنَا وَٱجۡتَبَيۡنَآۚ إِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ خَرُّواْۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ وَبُكِيࣰّ ا۩
19:58.en: These are they unto whom Allah showed favour from among the prophets, of the seed of Adam and of those whom We carried (in the ship) with Noah, and of the seed of Abraham and Israel, and from among those whom We guided and chose. When the revelations of the Beneficent were recited unto them, they fell down, adoring and weeping

19:59.ar: ۞فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفٌ أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِۖ فَسَوۡفَ يَلۡقَوۡنَ غَيًّا
19:59.en: Now there hath succeeded them a later generation whom have ruined worship and have followed lusts. But they will meet deception

19:60.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:60.en: Save him who shall repent and believe and do right. Such will enter the Garden, and they will not be wronged in aught

19:61.ar: جَنَّٰتِ عَدۡنٍ ٱلَّتِي وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ عِبَادَهُۥ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ وَعۡدُهُۥ مَأۡتِيࣰّ ا
19:61.en: Gardens of Eden, which the Beneficent hath promised to His slaves in the unseen. Lo! His promise is ever sure of fulfilment

19:66.ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ أَءِذَا مَا مِتُّ لَسَوۡفَ أُخۡرَجُ حَيًّا
19:66.en: And man saith: When I am dead, shall I forsooth be brought forth alive

19:67.ar: أَوَلَا يَذۡكُرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰهُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَلَمۡ يَكُ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:67.en: Doth not man remember that We created him before, when he was naught

19:68.ar: فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحۡشُرَنَّهُمۡ وَٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحۡضِرَنَّهُمۡ حَوۡلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيࣰّ ا
19:68.en: And, by thy Lord, verily We shall assemble them and the devils, then We shall bring them, crouching, around hell

19:69.ar: ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمۡ أَشَدُّ عَلَى ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ عِتِيࣰّ ا
19:69.en: Then We shall pluck out from every sect whichever of them was most stubborn in rebellion to the Beneficent

19:70.ar: ثُمَّ لَنَحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهَا صِلِيࣰّ ا
19:70.en: And surely We are Best Aware of those most worthy to be burned therein

19:71.ar: وَإِن مِّنكُمۡ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَاۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتۡمࣰ ا مَّقۡضِيࣰّ ا
19:71.en: There is not one of you but shall approach it. That is a fixed ordinance of thy Lord

19:72.ar: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَواْ وَّنَذَرُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيࣰّ ا
19:72.en: Then We shall rescue those who kept from evil, and leave the evil-doers crouching there

19:81.ar: وَٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةࣰ لِّيَكُونُواْ لَهُمۡ عِزࣰّ ا
19:81.en: And they have chosen (other) gods beside Allah that they may be a power for them

19:82.ar: كَلَّاۚ سَيَكۡفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمۡ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ضِدًّا
19:82.en: Nay, but they will deny their worship of them, and become opponents unto them

19:83.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمۡ أَزࣰّ ا
19:83.en: Seest thou not that We have set the devils on the disbelievers to confound them with confusion

19:84.ar: فَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمۡ عَدࣰّ ا
19:84.en: So make no haste against them (O Muhammad). We do but number unto them a sum (of days)

19:85.ar: يَوۡمَ نَحۡشُرُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَفۡدࣰ ا
19:85.en: On the day when We shall gather the righteous unto the Beneficent, a goodly company

19:86.ar: وَنَسُوقُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرۡدࣰ ا
19:86.en: And drive the guilty unto hell, a weary herd

19:88.en: And they say: The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son

19:89.en: Assuredly ye utter a disastrous thing

19:90.ar: تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرۡنَ مِنۡهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلۡجِبَالُ هَدًّا
19:90.en: Whereby almost the heavens are torn, and the earth is split asunder and the mountains fall in ruins

19:91.en: That ye ascribe unto the Beneficent a son

19:92.ar: وَمَا يَنۢبَغِي لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا
19:92.en: When it is not meet for (the Majesty of) the Beneficent that He should choose a son

19:93.ar: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِي ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ عَبۡدࣰ ا
19:93.en: There is none in the heavens and the earth but cometh unto the Beneficent as a slave

19:94.en: Verily He knoweth them and numbereth them with (right) numbering

19:95.en: And each one of them will come unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone

19:96.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَيَجۡعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وُدࣰّ ا
19:96.en: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love

19:97.ar: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرۡنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنذِرَ بِهِۦ قَوۡمࣰ ا لُّدࣰّ ا
19:97.en: And We make (this Scripture) easy in thy tongue, (O Muhammad) only that thou mayst bear good tidings therewith unto those who ward off (evil), and warn therewith the froward folk

19:98.ar: وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّن قَرۡنٍ هَلۡ تُحِسُّ مِنۡهُم مِّنۡ أَحَدٍ أَوۡ تَسۡمَعُ لَهُمۡ رِكۡزَۢا
19:98.en: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed! Canst thou (Muhammad) see a single man of them, or hear from them the slightest sound

U8TjKPN8Ac8.title: A Juz A Day, Juz 16 Part 2: Surah Maryam, Faith and Family
U8TjKPN8Ac8.one_line: A walk through Surah Maryam: families of faith from Zakariyya and Maryam to Ibrahim, how faith shapes family life, and the Day of Regret.
U8TjKPN8Ac8.summary: Moving from the end of al-Kahf into Surah Maryam, he reads the surah as a gallery of families of faith. Zakariyya prays quietly in old age and is given Yahya, with a sign of three days of silence; Yahya is praised for wisdom as a child and kindness to his parents. Maryam withdraws, receives the angel, and in labour is told to shake the palm trunk, which he notes no one could really shake; the lesson is that we do our part and Allah provides. Eating and drinking calm her before she faces her people in silence and lets the infant speak. He observes that these families suffered for their faith, yet half of humanity still names children after them. He dwells on Ibrahim's appeal to his idolatrous father, built on logic and affection with each sentence opening 'O my father', and his gentle farewell, noting that faith can strain family ties and that this is acceptable as long as faith is upheld. He then moves through Musa, Harun, Isma'il and Idris, the Day of Regret, the passing over the Fire, the honoured gathering of the God-fearing, and the gravity of ascribing a son to the Most Compassionate.

outline.heading: Opening
Zakariyya's quiet prayer in old age
outline.gist: With white hair and a barren wife, Zakariyya calls on his Lord privately, never having been disappointed in his prayers.

outline.heading: Good news of Yahya
outline.gist: He is given a son with a name no one had before; Allah, who created him from nothing, finds this easy.

outline.heading: The sign of silence
outline.gist: Though healthy, he speaks to people only by signs for three days, a miraculous sign to the community.

outline.heading: Yahya: wisdom as a child, kind to his parents
outline.gist: Given judgment while young, compassion and purity, and dutiful to his parents; peace on him in life and death.

outline.heading: Maryam's seclusion and the angel
outline.gist: She seeks refuge in the Most Merciful from the stranger, who tells her he comes to grant her a pure son, a decree already settled.

outline.heading: Labour at the palm trunk
outline.gist: Driven to the trunk by pain, she wishes she had died before this, and is reassured from below her.

outline.heading: Shake the trunk: do your part
outline.gist: No one can truly shake a palm trunk, yet she was told to; we do the best we can and Allah supplies the result.

outline.heading: Eat, drink and be at ease; the vow of silence
outline.gist: Eating and drinking have a calming effect in distress; then she lets the baby answer for her.

outline.heading: The infant speaks
outline.gist: Accused by her people, she points to the child, who declares himself Allah's servant and prophet, blessed and dutiful to his mother.

outline.heading: That is Isa son of Maryam
outline.gist: The word of truth about him; when Allah decrees a thing He says Be, and it is.

outline.heading: Families of faith who suffered for it
outline.gist: These families lived and suffered for their faith, yet half of humanity still names children after them; the sects differed about Isa.

outline.heading: The Day of Regret
outline.gist: When the matter is settled, those who turned away will see the truth while having lived in heedlessness.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's appeal to his father
outline.gist: He asks why his father worships what cannot see or help, and offers to guide him on a straight path.

outline.heading: Logic and love: 'O my father'
outline.gist: Each appeal begins with tender address; he uses reason and affection and warns out of concern for his father.

outline.heading: When faith strains family ties
outline.gist: Threatened and sent away, Ibrahim answers with peace and a promise to seek forgiveness; family dynamics may suffer, but faith must be upheld.

outline.heading: Musa and Harun
outline.gist: Musa called from the right side of the mountain and drawn near, with his brother Harun given to him as a prophet.

outline.heading: Isma'il and Idris
outline.gist: Isma'il was true to his promise and enjoined prayer on his family; Idris was truthful and raised high.

outline.heading: Prostrating in tears, then successors who followed desires
outline.gist: The prophets fell down weeping when the revelation was recited; later generations neglected prayer and followed desire.

outline.heading: 'Will I really be raised when I die?'
outline.gist: Allah created the human before, when he was nothing.

outline.heading: Everyone passes over it; the God-fearing are saved
outline.gist: Those who rejected their Lord for frivolous desires are brought around the Fire; the passing is a decree, then the God-fearing are rescued.

outline.heading: False gods disown their worshippers
outline.gist: Those they took as gods will deny them; devils spur the disbelievers on, and their days are counted.

outline.heading: The God-fearing gathered as honoured guests
outline.gist: The righteous are brought to the Most Compassionate as an honoured delegation, while the guilty are driven to Hell.

outline.heading: The heavens nearly burst at the claim of a son
outline.gist: Ascribing a child to the Most Compassionate is so monstrous that heavens, earth and mountains almost collapse.

outline.heading: Love for believers and a Quran made easy
outline.gist: Allah will place affection for those who believe and do good; the Quran is made easy to give glad tidings and warning.

outline.heading: Outro
